I am writing to formally lodge a complaint regarding the practices of all banking and lenders run this same issue however I am specifically talking about my situation with plaza home mortgage. concerning the endorsement of loan documents and the subsequent financial implications that are not disclosed to borrowers. I believe these practices may violate the principles of transparency and fairness as intended by the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) and other consumer protection regulations. Lack of Disclosure on Endorsements It has come to my attention that when signing loan documents, borrowers, including myself, are not informed about the different types of indorsements and their potential uses by the lender. Specifically, the use of blank endorsements on these documents allows the lender to transform them into negotiable instruments. These negotiable instruments can then be utilized to secure funds from the Federal Reserve or other financial entities, often with collateral requirements as low as 10 %. Financial Implications and Transparency This practice effectively enables lenders to obtain substantial funds from these endorsed documents without the borrower 's knowledge or consent. The funds obtained through these negotiable instruments are not applied towards reducing the borrowers loan or purchase amount. Instead, they are retained by the lender, often classified as a " gift '' on the books, thereby increasing the lenders financial gain at the expense of the borrower. Regulatory and Legal Considerations Under the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), lenders are mandated to provide clear and comprehensive disclosures about the cost of credit, including the annual percentage rate ( APR ), finance charges, amount financed, and the total amount of payments. While TILA does not specifically address the issue of document endorsements, the broader principle of transparency and fairness should encompass the full range of financial implications related to the loan. Case law, such as Rodash v. XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX Cir. XXXX ), underscores the necessity of full disclosure under TILA. In this case, the court emphasized the importance of clear and complete disclosures to prevent unfair practices. Similarly, in In re Bassett, 285 F.3d 882 ( 9th Cir. 2002 ), the court ruled in favor of the borrower due to the lenders failure to provide adequate disclosures, reinforcing the necessity for lenders to fully inform borrowers of all terms and conditions. Request for Resolution Given the concerns outlined above, I respectfully request the following actions : Full Disclosure : That plaza home mortgage and whomever else provides full and clear disclosure to borrowers regarding the types of endorsements on loan documents and their potential financial implications. Review and Adjustment : That any funds obtained through the use of negotiable instruments derived from my loan documents be reviewed and I have already paid this loan off in full but i fee I am entitled to any funds and interest obtained or gained by my blank endorsement as I was not properly informed of all options or that they would use my document to obtain any additional funds at my expense. Policy Changes : That plaza home mortgage implement policy changes to ensure future borrowers are fully informed about the endorsement process and its potential impact on their loan obligations. I believe these steps are necessary to align with the spirit of XXXX and to uphold the principles of fairness and transparency in lending practices. I look forward to your prompt response and resolution of this matter. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX References to Consider : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, 16 F.3d 1142 ( 11th Cir. 1994 ) : Case emphasizing the necessity of full disclosure under XXXX. In re XXXX, 285 F.3d 882 ( 9th Cir. 2002 ) : Case highlighting the importance of adequate disclosures to prevent unfair practices.

Strong Protections for Struggling Borrowers The CFPBs mortgage servicing rules ensure that borrowers in trouble get a fair process to avoid foreclosure. Borrowers shouldnt have to worry about mortgage servicers cutting corners or losing applications for relief. They should be told about their options and given time to apply and be considered for loan modifications and other alternatives. Most of all, they shouldnt be surprised by the start of a foreclosure proceeding until they have had time to explore all available options. If they act diligently to seek alternatives, they should not face a foreclosure sale before their applications have been evaluated. The new protections for struggling borrowers include : Restricted Dual-Tracking : Under the CFPBs new rules, dual-tracking when the servicer moves forward with foreclosure while simultaneously working with the borrower to avoid foreclosure is restricted. Servicers can not start a foreclosure proceeding if a borrower has already submitted a complete application for a loan modification or other alternative to foreclosure, and that application is still pending review. To give borrowers reasonable time to submit such applications, servicers can not make the first notice or filing required for the foreclosure process until a mortgage loan account is more than 120 days delinquent.

Here is a recap of my nightmarish experience with ServiceMac LLC ( SM ) during the pandemic : SM advised me that there was no cost to enter into the forbearance arrangement and that they were here to help. In fact, almost all of your correspondence says that but I soon found out that this was just feel-good language that you use but it had nothing to do with reality as your customers could not reach you ; if I did get thru I was told that it would be XXXX days before I could receive a callback. SM encouraged its customers/me to send partial payments whenever I was able. I did so for some months because I wanted to show a good faith effort on my part and also to minimize my financial burden after the forbearance period. Unfortunately for me, all SM did was XXXX up my $ XXXX partial payments ( half of my normal monthly mortgage payment ) with what appears to be largely made-up fees. At XXXX point, SM wrote to me saying that I had an escrow shortage due to an increase in my hazard/homeowners insurance. I asked by phone and by email for SM to apply the recent partial payment to the shortage. I always pay escrow shortages upfront, I did this XXXX with XXXX XXXX then XXXX XXXX. I prefer not to roll over escrow shortages into my loan to avoid interest charged on it for years to come. Your company just ignored my pleas. Finally after weeks of asking, XXXX of your reps said that it could not be done while I was in a forbearance. I kept appealing but to this day I do not know if the shortage was rolled into my loan or not. SM assigned to me more than a half a dozen SPOCs ( single point of contact ) during the forbearance period, a paradox in itself, none of whom I ever spoke with except XXXX. Frustrating is the nicest way that I can describe the lack of continuity and lack of follow-up or follow-through from SM. For weeks at a time, both your Customer Service and Loss Mitigation departments were completely inaccessible to me- the CUSTOMER. When I finally did get a call back or pressed until I got a warm body, your reps did NOT provide any tangible help, just more rhetoric. It became apparent that your Customer Service staff was painfully ill-equipped to handle the needs of your customers during the pandemic. Extremely dissatisfied with SMs lack of responses or answers, I contacted XXXX directly for guidance since this was/is a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. A Finance & Loan Analyst there explained XXXX possible approaches that mortgage companies were given to utilize as forbearance exit strategies for their customers. I wrote down each approach with the details as he broke them down for me, answering my questions as I asked him. Yet, when I contacted SM to review these approaches, your company told me that a team of experts reviewed my situation and came up with the best and ONLY exit strategy for me. Best for who? At that point I told your rep that I had XXXX years as a personal finance consultant and teaching debtor education programs. I assured SM I was more than competent to be a part of that conversation and decision. The only response I got to my assertion was that if I did not sign the proposed loan modification, I could face negative consequences going forward since I could not make the lump sum payment to bring my account current. SM would not offer me an option to extend the forbearance another XXXX months once they drafted the modification. Still desperate, I asked SM reps if they knew of any government programs offering help to people like me. I was hearing on the news that such programs were being implemented. SM said No but I believe you all were not forthcoming about this. This is your industry, your line of work and you dont know anything! All you wanted was the hefty profit afforded you through the greedy loan modification you devised and pressured me to sign. I wanted the financial assistance that was available to me because the funds would have brought my account completely current allowing me to get back on track, just as these programs did for so many others. Asking for assistance was rare for me. I am not the type of person who looks for hand-outs, Ive been working since I was XXXX ; I am now XXXX years of age. In the end, SM did NOT abide by any of the guidelines set forth by XXXX. I advised your organization that I was NOT comfortable signing the loan modification agreement without speaking with your so-called experts who devised it- to get my questions answered and my concerns addressed. I knew right off the bat that this agreement was exploitative. Somehow over the next few weeks, SM could contact me more to convince me to sign this unfair loan modification. Your organization practically coerced me into signing it, knowing I did not have many options and hinting at foreclosure as a possible consequence. Unfortunately for me, I did not learn about the specifics of the federal assistance programs and the Louisiana XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX until after I signed it. This meant I no longer qualified since my mortgage account was technically no longer past due. Had I not been so overwhelmed with taking care of my senior mom at the time who was coming to the end stage of life, Im sure I would have fought this longer. I feel like I deprived my mother of some medical supplies and equipment she desperately needed, wanting to do the right thing by making partial monthly payments to SM. A decision I greatly regret in my grief. For SM to state that the capitalization amount in the loan modification was {$10000.00} provided good optics but the truth is the original loan maturity date on my fixed rate mortgage was XX/XX/year>. So for a forbearance period of a little more than a year, your modification extended my maturity date to XXXX of XXXX adding XXXX months to the life of my loan and thereby increasing my mortgage debt by roughly {$52000.00}! In retrospect, it appears SM was playing a game of evasion with your customers while your Loss Mitigation team cooked up ways to considerably profit off of us who were in the middle of a crisis. Wouldnt it have been more ethical to first recoup the interest that was halted during forbearance, then tack on the months the mortgage was not paid during forbearance and charge reasonable fees for doing so? Not surprising, right after your big windfall, SM simply transferred/sold my mortgage to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. The idea that mortgage lenders need liquidity to continue to lend is understandable. But the idea that mortgage servicers can easily and continually profit by packaging and selling loans, means there is absolutely no loyalty to your customers- the mortgagors, because we are a temporary to you ; no reason to provide a good customer experience because we are temporary to you. This short term arrangement almost assures that we as debtors have no means to hold ServiceMac and other mortgage companies accountable for rotten service and unscrupulous activities. However, I am making sure that the Consumer Protection Financial Bureau is watching you. Your company is a debt collector not a service provider and it is wrong for you to tout the untruthful message that you care and you're here to help as we are merely transient debtors to you. So spare me! The pandemic created unprecedented times for both companies and citizens and I took that into consideration with SM but concluded after several months of XXXX ; the name ServiceMac is seriously misleading and I will only agree that SM is a subservicing business if sub stands for below par. Please note that if you have completed a refinance of your original loan the XXXX year requirement resets to the XXXX payment date of your refinanced loan. Please note that all appraisals must be ordered through our offices and are at the expense of the property owner. Per your loans investor requirements, appraisals for PMI removal purposes must be ordered through an unbiased third-party appraisal company approved by the servicer. In order to make certain that we are in compliance with investor requirements, only appraisals ordered through our offices will be acceptable for PMI removal purposes. Please do not send us an appraisal report that was ordered outside of our offices as we will not be able to accept it for PMI removal purposes. We can not take into account local market trends, tax assessments or home value websites as evidence to order an appraisal or to change the LTV. If you have completed substantial STRUCTURAL improvements ( i.e. an addition put on the property or other combined substantial improvements ), please send specifics including what improvements were made, materials used and costs excluding labor. We are requesting this information so we can determine if you are eligible to receive the pre-2 year appraisal information. Loans that are granted the early appraisal, due to approved substantial STRUCTURAL improvements, will only require an 80.00 % LTV for PMI removal eligibility. Loans that are between 2-5 years will need to show a LTV of 75.00 % or 25.00 % equity from an appraisal. If the improvements do not meet the requirements, then you must wait two years to have an appraisal done. With any appraisal, it is possible that the value of the property in question may show an increase in value, but also may in fact show a decrease in value. What are substantial structural improvements? A substantial structural improvement is typically renovations that substantially improve marketability and substantially extend the useful life of the property. This can be a replacement of a major component ( i.e. kitchen renovations replacing cabinet and countertops or bathroom renovation replacing bathroom tile or bathtub ) or significant structural alteration to the property ( i.e. relocating walls, adding additional living space, finishing a basement, garage, deck, or in-ground pool. What are not structural improvements? Cosmetic improvements are not considered structural improvements and will not affect the property value as much as structural improvements. Repairs that are made to keep the property maintained and fully functional are not considered improvements. Cosmetic improvements include : new paint, new siding, a new roof, new carpeting, new flooring, landscaping, new windows, new light fixtures, new appliances or a new heating/air conditioning unit. If you believe that you may be eligible for a pre-2-year appraisal, please email or mail details of the improvements preformed ( in the below/attached format ) and if possible include proof of the cost of improvements ( i.e. receipts or work orders ) in order for us to determine your eligibility. text: My mortgage loan was transferred effective XX/XX/XXXX, which was about halfway between the XX/XX/XXXX official due date and the end of the grace period- XXXX XXXX on which I was planning to make my payment with the original servicer, Guaranteed Rate. I called Shellpoint- the new servicer- shortly after I got the letter advising of the transfer, and informed them of the uncertainty regarding the status of the autopay. The agent I spoke to told me it is totally fine to wait and see if that pulls, since I have a 60-day grace period to make my payments. I was surprised by this generous time frame, and it occurred to me that if I really had a 60 day grace period, I might be able to earn some interest on the funds by waiting until nearly the 60th day to make both the XXXX and XXXX payments. I asked the agent to confirm whether the grace period would allow me to do so without an issue. She balked a bit, and clearly had never been asked that question before. She asked me to wait on a brief hold while she confirmed that with her supervisor. She eventually came back and said that, yes, I could wait until XXXX at the end of the grace period to make my XXXX and XXXX payments ( assuming they didn't get processed by the Guaranteed Rate autopay ), and that would be fine. I thanked her for her help. Finding the long grace period to be perhaps almost too good to be true, I looked up the Federal regulations regarding mortgage servicing transfers, and found that they only protect mortgagees from certain consequences in the event payments are made on time to the original servicer, and arrive late via forwarding to the new servicer. I received a call from another agent on XX/XX/XXXX looking to secure a payment on the account. I relayed to him what I'd been told by the first agent about 6 weeks earlier, but told him that I had been meaning to call anyway out of an abundance of caution. I told him that I had been told there was a grace period running until on or about XX/XX/XXXX, and that because I was told it would not cause me any fees, penalties, or negative credit reporting if I held onto the funds until the 60 days had run, I was planning to pay on or around XX/XX/XXXX. But I added that I'd looked into the regulations which don't require such generous treatment, and that while I had him on the phone, I'd like to confirm that Shellpoint 's policy allows for a grace period of 60 days as I'd been advised. He told me that it's not technically a grace period, and that the other agent should not have used those words. I then said ( at least almost verbatim ) " okay, but just to be clear, my understanding from her is that there would be no negative consequences to my paying my XXXX and XXXX payments, so long as it was done fewer than 60 days after the transfer date. Can you confirm that? '' He then confirmed that there would be no consequences, and asked if I'd like to set up a payment for XXXX, which I did ( though I later cancelled and set up the payment from a different account ). I then began receiving mailings about my " defaulted mortgage, '' but knew based on these two conversations that I didn't need to worry about it. But then I got a {$19.00} fee for property inspection. Bringing back the pre-payment penalty to homeowners seeking conventional long-term home loans : My sincere opinion on this subject seems fair and reasonable. It takes much time, talent and work to pull together successfully a home loan for any borrower. As a loan officer connected with a company for 24+ years and enduring much change in the lending world of consumer protection guidelines, it think that when a consumer chooses to pay off a long term mortgage loan inside of 6 months from the closing date, the consumer should be required to pay a pre-payment penalty that would equate to the costs and penalties equal to what lenders and loan officers currently are required to pay or pay back on an early payoff. The loan officer is a consumer too and works hard for their income in ever changing economic conditions. It seems only fair that the home owner should be held responsible for the costs incurred in an early payoff of a long-term conventional home loan. For that purpose, I propose that a 6 months pre-payment penalty should be brought back to the lending industry on Conventional home loans in disclosure regulations. I don't feel it fair to charge the loan officer and the company they represent for the early payoff costs when they sincerely help the home buyer with their goals of financing the purchase of their homes in a timely manner. A minimum Prepayment penalty can be there to bring knowledge to consumers that there is a Serious cost to providing a long-term home loan to consumers. Getting a home loan is Not Free. Lenders/Loan officers should not have to feel like their livelihood is in jeopardy when a consumer decides to pay off their mortgage inside of 6 months. We shouldn't be tasked to work for free. What professional industry is regulatorily tasked with paying back fairly earned income? Change the regulations.

In late XXXX, we experienced a significant, temporary loss of income and several concurrent major household expenses ( replacement of the whole house generator, paving a section of our driveway, furnace replacement, and replacement of our oven/microwave ). Recognizing the seriousness of the situation and with a deep desire to maintain our home, we contacted our servicer, AmeriHome Mortgage, to apply for temporary mitigation of our VA insured loan. The management of this process has been unduly delayed, haphazard, predatory, and damaging to our financial and professional wellbeing. In XXXX, I concluded that we were facing difficult circumstances and that my employment situation would take some months to reset. I sought assistance from AmeriHome Mortgage. Confident that we would recover, I based my estimate of assistance needed on the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Executives study that showed the average time to a new position for someone in my position is 18 months. In mid-XXXX XXXX, I requested to apply for mitigation. A packet was sent via USPS, dated XXXX XXXX and a duplicate emailed on XXXX XXXX. I then submitted a Mortgage Assistance Application. On XXXX XXXX, a request for supporting documents was sent to us. These documents were provided and on XXXX XXXX, the application was resubmitted and receipt acknowledged. At this time, we estimated the financial difficulties would resolve within six months. During this time, delinquency letters were sent, dated XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, and XXXX XXXX. While cause for concern, I was confident that this would not be an issue because I was proactively in contact with our loan servicer and taking steps to resolve our circumstances in a positive manner. We subsequently received a letter stating : Your application is complete as of XX/XX/XXXX and no further information is needed at this time. While a weighty concern, I was confident in a successful resolution. We subsequently received, on XXXX XXXX, both the HUD notice of potential foreclosure and a notice of default that offered options for mitigation options I had already pursued. This was followed by another notice of pending foreclosure on XXXX XXXX and a XXXX XX/XX/XXXX correspondence offering options to cure the delinquency. Curious as to the status of our application, I called customer service on XXXX XX/XX/XXXX and was advised to call back the following week. During my XXXX XX/XX/XXXX call, I was informed that it would take a week to ten days for a decision for be forthcoming. This exchange would be repeated multiple times over the coming months, with my being advised each time that a decision would be forthcoming within days. In late XX/XX/XXXX, we were again requested to file a Uniform Borrower Assistance Form and to resubmit supporting documents that had expired while in the servicers queue. These were provided on XXXX XXXX. On XXXX XXXX, receipt of the second application was provided, replacing the same information that was termed as expired by the servicer. At this time, we indicated the expected length of the financial difficulty would be 6 to 12 months. Later that month, we were again requested to submit another Uniform Borrows Assistance Form, providing for the fourth time essentially the same information. On XXXX XXXX, we were again advised that our application was complete. On XXXX XXXX, we were happy to receive notice of granting of a three-month forbearance, but alarmed that the grace period was only for XXXX to the end of XXXX. This ignored the period XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX, which is within the period of mitigation application. This also resulted in our loan being reported as greater than 90 days delinquent, despite our haven taken steps to facilitate a positive outcome. On XXXX XX/XX/XXXX, I sent, via email to XXXX, an inquiry about the period between when I applied for mitigation and when a decision was reached. I did not receive either acknowledgement of receipt or a response until automated telephone calls began at the end of XXXX. I contacted the servicer and was told that, even though we ha requested mitigation, ( 1 ) the credit report record of delinquency would stand because payments were not rendered and ( 2 ) the delay in adjudication was due to incomplete or expired information. When I pointed out that the supporting documents were submitted, I was told they were not. I further inquired regarding the three month forbearance versus the 6 to 12 month period of difficulty and was told I would have to file another application for mitigation to take effect after the three month forbearance ended on XXXX XX/XX/XXXX. On XXXX XX/XX/XXXX, we submitted a fifth Uniform Borrower Assistance Form with attachments. During the first week in XXXX, we received yet another request for submission of a Uniform Borrower Assistance Form and supporting documents. These were provided -- for the sixth time. Also note that in XXXX, AmeriHome reported the mortgage 150 days late, despite this being within the approved forbearance period. Documents demonstrating these activities are enclosed with this filing. One might assume that the purpose of loan mitigation is to allow continuation of home ownership. It is counterproductive, then, to delay decision on a request initiated in XXXX until XXXX, then deny any forbearance for that period. Nor is the utility evident of granting a three month forbearance for a problem projected to last for six to twelve months ; and reporting an increase in delinquency during the forbearance. We ask for positive consideration for several cogent reasons. The primary reason is that we hold significant equity in our home. Our current balance is approximately {$800000.00}. Our home was recently appraised by the county at approximately {$1.00} XXXX, more than enough to support a home equity line of credit to make the mortgage current with a single payment. Of note, a similar home, but with fewer amenities, immediately next door sold on XXXX XX/XX/XXXX for {>= $1,000,000}. The problem is no lender will offer a note to someone with a 150 day mortgage delinquency. I have been actively and aggressively seeking gainful employment in an amazingly competitive market. I have been able to secure increased income, but it will take 30 to 60 days to become effective. We occupy our home, our primary and only residence. We greatly wish to retain ownership and to return to currency on our mortgage. When I spoke with AmeriHome customer service on XXXX XXXX, I was informed that the decision on mitigation was delayed because the application was incomplete. This is neither accurate nor seemingly fair. The acknowledgements of receipt repeatedly stated that the application was complete, as noted above. The submissions and supporting documents were essentially identical each time. While we were unable to fulfil our financial obligations at the time, we also reached out in a timely manner to secure alternative arrangements as specified on the servicers web site. The lack of progress on adjudication in the face of our temporary inability to meet our obligations has rendered us unable to recover for the foreseeable future. It has also had a cascading negative effect on our credit and finances. Several lines of credit have been closed, which, in turn, reduces our credit scores. Moreover, my wife is in the final six months of her graduate program that will improve our financial status. Her federally guaranteed student loan was denied due to the 90 day delinquency ( letter enclosed ). Left unresolved, she will not be able to complete her studies. Loss of our home would not adversely impact our servicer, as that obligation would easily be met should we be forced to leave this property. It would, however, have a decidedly adverse impact on us as a family. While I recognize that the mortgage company is not a charity, one would hope the lender could offer flexibility to allow continued home ownership, acknowledging that the lender suffers no damage as we remain liable for accumulated interest during the forbearance. Put colloquially, we did our part to navigate an unfortunate situation. We would hope the lender could do the same. We ask that the forbearance period begin when it was requested and the adverse credit report be withdrawn. This will allow us to secure a HELOC and make this account current. Respectfully,

In XXXX of XXXX I reported an over {$10000.00} health and safety error and omission in my FHA appraisal that would have disqualified the home from funding. I have since learned HUD and the FHA rely on the lender to not only self report errors, but they allow them to choose the severity category out of the XXXX XXXX XXXX choices, some of which having lesser penalties than others. Cardinal Financial chose the category of property eligibility rather than property appraisal because the category of property appraisal incriminates appraiser and/or underwriter and is a severity level of 2 requiring Mitigating Documentation OR Indemnification Life-of-Loan and states FHA is unable to determine appraiser and/or underwriter compliance with applicable policies for the appraisal, collateral valuation, or property acceptability due to absence of valid documentation. FHA is able to conclude that the property was not appraised and/or underwritten in compliance with applicable policies and the appraised value is not supported or the property is not acceptable as a result. Documentation required for specific property types, programs/products, or by construction status was not obtained to support FHA max insurable loan amount. Due to Cardinal Financial choosing the incorrect category and not checking the box for Fraud in the self-report system, FHA prematurely excused them with the following that Cardinal used to close my initial complaint. FHA closed the review stating to the lender. Thank you for the self-report regarding the properties well and septic. FHA has taken the appropriate actions and has determined that lender could not have known about the well and septic prior to closing. No further action is required. It was classified as Tier 4 ( indicating that the Mortgagee did not know and could not have known ). Through two years and nine months of research, recent communication and policy updates from FHA commissioner XXXX XXXX proves that classification was wrong. " According to my team, they have looked into your situation multiple times and have determined that there is nothing HUD can do. They have advised you to file a complaint with your state regulators. While I have asked them to go back to look again, I do not have any reason to believe the answer will be different, and unfortunately another inquiry will likely take at least several weeks at best and possibly longer. Have you filed a complaint with state regulators, the CFPB, the Appraisal Foundation, or anyone else besides HUD? '' Sincerely yours, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Secretary for Housing and Federal Housing Commissioner U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development XXXX XXXX She also issued the following update to the Defect Taxonomy requiring fraud and misrepresentation be classified as a severity level 1 not 4. Effective Date The provisions of this ML are effective immediately. All updates will be incorporated into a forthcoming update of the HUD Handbook XXXX, FHA Single Family Housing Policy Handbook ( Handbook XXXX ). Affected Programs The provisions of this ML apply to all FHA Title II Single Family mortgage programs. Background The FHA Defect Taxonomy ( Handbook XXXX, Appendix XXXX ) is FHAs quality assurance framework for Title II loan reviews. It provides a consistent method for identifying defects at the loan level, useful data and feedback through structured categorization of defects, and balance between FHAs statutory obligation to mitigate risk to the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) and quality assurance business processes. Mortgagee Letter XXXX, Continued 2 The Fraud or Misrepresentation section of the FHA Defect Taxonomy currently states that Findings of fraud or materially misrepresented information can fall into one of two severity tiers : Tier 1 ( indicating that the Mortgagee knew or should have known ), or Tier 4 ( indicating that the Mortgagee did not know and could not have known ). It further states that FHA determines if the Mortgagee knew or should have known based on whether : An employee of the Mortgagee was involved, and/or Red flags in the loan file that should have been questioned by the underwriting Mortgagee. Mortgagees are responsible for the actions of their sponsored TPOs under 24 CFR 202.8 ( a ) ( XXXX ) and XXXX XXXX Section I.A.5.a.v. To better align the Defect Taxonomy with these existing requirements and mitigate risk to the MMIF, FHA is updating the Defect Taxonomy to include fraud or material misrepresentation involving a sponsored TPO as one of the knew or should have known conditions used by FHA to determine whether a Tier 1 severity classification is appropriate. Based on this update, FHA will seek life-of-loan indemnification from Mortgagees when there is evidence of fraud or material misrepresentation involving a sponsored TPO, regardless of whether FHA identifies specific red flags that should have been questioned at underwriting. Please review my initial complaint using the most recent update which requires the lender to mitigate.

Per the XXXX XXXX Revised Code, XXXX OCCUPANCY PERMIT ; CERTIFICATE OF COMPLETION [ A ] XXXX : Use and Occupancy : A building or structure shall not be used or occupied, and a change in the existing use or occupancy classification of a building or structure or portion thereof shall not be made, until the building official has issued a certificate of occupancy therefore as provided herein. XXXX XXXX Revised Code [ A ] XXXX My mortgage company has been aware that we can not legally occupy the property for which we have a mortgage, per the City of XXXX, just as in the XXXX matter. I've just completed my first year of a 30-year mortgage that is being serviced by NewRez LLC ( c/o Shellpoint Mortgage Servicing ). I called again on XX/XX/XXXX, spoke to an apologetic customer service agent who acknowledged documentation of my first call and that the issue had be researched by their escrow department. She connected me to what I understood to be a more specialized agent. This agent seemed to contradict statements of the first and was generally more defensive of the situation and process than the first. I left the call highly uncertain about the status of the escrow and indicated to both agents my intent to file this complaint. On XX/XX/XXXX, I received an email from NewRez indicating that may payment would be increasing. The email contained a link to a " personalized video '' that cheerfully indicated to me that my escrow account was underfunded by {$2400.00} and that my monthly payment would increase by {$220.00} to cover the difference. By virtue of my education, employment and experience with mortgage issues, I consider myself a more savvy consumer with regard to these matters. My biggest concern involving NewRez 's systems, procedures and processes is the potential impact on other customers who have NOT caught similar issues and will begin paying, or are already paying, higher payments than are in fact owed to NewRez due to similar accounting failures as I have experienced with the company. My complaint involves three concerns : 1 ) NewRez has demonstrated critical flaws in the accuracy of their Escrow Accounting process that have resulted in critical inconsistencies in the information provided to me and that have repeatedly represented that I owe more money to them than I in fact owe. This has also led to the depletion of my Escrow account over the past year for PMI charges that both parties admit I do not owe. 2 ) NewRez has failed to prevent the continued relaying of inaccurate information about my escrow status in the 16 days following my initial call to bring the matter to their attention, resulting in my continued distress, confusion and time wasted calling their servicing department. 3 ) NewRez 's initial failure and subsequent handling of the situation make me concerned that this may be part of a broader issue with their accounting policies and procedures, which could only be rectified with an audit of these processes.

text: Allow me to begin by stating that my husband and I have been loyal customers of Wells Fargo for a number of years. For XXXX years, all accounts serviced by them have been jointly owned by me and my husband. My husband passed away XXXX years ago. Until recently, I had not notified Wells Fargo of his death. On or about XX/XX/year>, I received XXXX letters from Wells Fargo both addressed to my husband. The letters explained that a recent review of accounts indicated that a service/product had been added to our mortgage account without authorization ( XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX ). Additionally, each letter referenced a different tracking number. On or about XX/XX/year>, I contacted, by phone, Wells Fargo XXXX XXXX. I explained that I had received XXXX letters and questioned why the letters were addressed only to my husband when our account was and had always been jointly owned. I further explained that my husband was now deceased. The representative asked for my name and questioned if I was authorized to act on my husbands ' behalf. I stated yes and provided my full name. She proceeded to explain that a check would be issued as compensation for the unauthorized addition of the products. She went on to state the amount to be compensated as related to each tracking number and that the checks would be received in approximately XXXX days. On or about XX/XX/year>, I received a XXXX letter from Wells Fargo. This letter was also addressed to my husband, also referenced a product/service that was added without authorization, and also referenced a different tracking number. That same day, I contacted Wells Fargo. I explained that my husband was deceased and stated that this product was unknowingly added to our account. The representative asked my name and I provided the information. She stated that a check would be issued in approximately XXXX days and she stated the amount of the check. Sometime in early XXXX, I received XXXX letters, each included a check pertaining to the initial XXXX letters I received XX/XX/year>. The checks issued in the amount of {$270.00} and {$410.00}, were both made payable only to my husband. About a week later, perhaps XXXX, I received a XXXX letter and a third check which referenced the letter previously received on or about XX/XX/XXXX. The check was issued for {$15.00}, a significantly smaller amount than the first XXXX. Additionally and more importantly, the check was issued to me. As I had recently removed my husband 's name from a joint banking account, the bank would not accept the checks made payable to him. I contacted Wells Fargo on XX/XX/year> and asked that the checks be reissued and made payable to me. I received an email from XXXX XXXX which included a form to be submitted in addition to supporting documentation to reissue checks. That same day, I submitted the completed form. Additionally, I uploaded a copy of the state-issued death certificate, a copy of my marriage license, and my drivers license. I received confirmation of the submission. On XX/XX/XXXX I received an email stating " Incomplete supporting documents ''. No other explanation was included in the email. Once again, I contacted XXXX XXXX. The representative stated that I would need to provide a copy of a will or a small estate affidavit. I asked the representative to explain the need to have either of these documents to support the re-issuance of the checks. I cited the information for supporting documentation provided in the email under the heading " Reissue to new payee ( for example, spouse, heir, next of kin ) ''. The acceptable documentation listed -- " copy of death certificate and any official documentation that validates the new payee name for the check ( for example, a small estate affidavit in accordance with state law ) ''. I attempted to explain that the documents I submitted in addition to the death certificate, were both state-issued, legal documents which validated my name. I further explained that the email did not state that a small estate affidavit was required, only given as an example. When I explained about the third check being issued to me and not my deceased husband, I was told it was because the amount of the check being so small ( {$15.00} ), they did not require additional documents. I have spoken with the XXXX department several times. They have stated that the checks would not be reissued to me without the affidavit. The court and legal cost to get such a document would be as much, if not more, than the value of the XXXX checks. Aside from that, the emailed instructions were not clear in stating that a small estate affidavit was required supporting documentation. Furthermore, I informed the XXXX XXXX representative in my initial conversations that my husband was deceased.

Detailed Explanation : I have been a tenant at the property located at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXXyXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX since XX/XX/XXXX. According to public records, the property owner, XXXX XXXX, acquired the property with a New Conventional Loan from XXXX XXXX. However, the timeline of events suggests that the property was never occupied by the borrower as a primary residence. Instead, it was rented out to me almost immediately after the loan was secured. Reasons for Concern : Occupancy Fraud : The mortgage terms likely required the borrower to occupy the property as their primary residence. The immediate rental of the property raises concerns that the borrower may have misrepresented their intent to occupy the property, which could constitute occupancy fraud. Impact on Tenant Rights : As a tenant, I am directly affected by any fraudulent actions related to the mortgage. If the loan terms were violated, my lease and rights as a tenant could be compromised. Facing Unlawful Eviction : I am currently facing eviction from this property, which may be unlawful due to the suspected occupancy fraud. This eviction could be a direct result of the property owners potential violation of the mortgage terms, placing me in a precarious and unjust position. Request for Action : Given these concerns, I am requesting that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) investigate this matter to determine if the mortgage terms were violated. Specifically, I request that the CFPB consider the following actions : Subpoena of Mortgage Documents : I request that LoanDepot.com LLC be subpoenaed to provide all relevant mortgage documents, including the original loan application and any related communications, to verify the occupancy requirements and whether they were violated. Investigation into Occupancy Fraud : I ask that a thorough investigation be conducted into the possibility of occupancy fraud and any related violations of federal lending laws. Protection of Tenant Rights : I seek assurance that my rights as a tenant are protected during this investigation, and that any actions taken by the property owner, including the eviction proceedings, are in full compliance with federal and state laws. Supporting Documentation : I am prepared to provide a copy of my rental agreement, communications with the property owner, and any other relevant documentation to support this complaint. Please let me know if there are additional steps I should take to assist with your investigation. Thank you for your attention to this serious matter. I look forward to your prompt response and any action the CFPB may take to address these concerns. Sincerely,

Dear CFPB, I am writing to formally lodge a complaint against my previous mortgage lender and servicer, XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, MERS, and Superior Loan Servicing. Despite this revision, none of the previously imposed fees were removed or adjusted, further exacerbating the financial burden placed on me. 4. Simultaneously, they initiated foreclosure proceedings against my property, compounding the stress and financial difficulty I was already facing. 5. Ongoing Financial and Emotional Impact The wrongful actions taken by my lender have not only caused me significant financial harm but have also subjected me to immense emotional distress. The combination of obstructive behavior, false reporting, and predatory lending practices has placed me in a precarious financial situation, with no immediate relief in sight. Their actions have not only violated my rights as a borrower but have also caused significant financial and emotional harm. I seek restitution for the damages incurred and request that the CFPB ensure that these practices do not continue to harm other consumers. Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your prompt response and intervention. Sincerely,

To : Mr. Cooper Attention Legal Department : I, XXXX XXXX, am writing in response to a letter I received on XX/XX/XXXX regarding the intent to foreclose on my property. On XX/XX/XXXX, I signed and issued a Promissory note to XXXX Mortgages. Shortly after closing, XXXX XXXX sold its rights to the note to Mr. Cooper. My note was converted into a draft made payable to Nationstar LLC. Since Mr. Cooper has previously identified itself as the holder in due course of this note, I hereby assert all claims and defenses that I have under the Uniform Commercial Code below. It has come to my attention that foreclosing my property will be in violation of the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC ), IRS Tax Standards, and Generally Accepted Accounting Principles ( GAAP ) as specified under 12 U.S.C. 1831n ( a ) ( 2 ) ( A ). Uniform Commercial Code According to the UCC, this Promissory Note is classified as : Negotiable Instrument ( UCC 3-104 ), and Collateral ( UCC 9-102 ( 12 ) ). While I was aware that I had granted a security interest in the property, it was not disclosed that I had also given security interest in a monetary instrument ( note ) according to 31 cfr.1010.100 ( dd ) upon transfer. Since this instrument is a monetary instrument, I am entitled to valuable consideration as it states in UCC 3-303. If an issuer of a promissory note does not receive valuable consideration, it has a defense. In addition, if an obligor signed an instrument without knowledge of the instrument 's character, it is also a defense under UCC 3-305. Under UCC 9-207, a secured party in possession or control of collateral : may hold as additional security any proceeds, except money or funds, received from the collateral. shall apply money or funds received from the collateral to reduce the secured obligation, unless remitted to the debtor ; and may create a security interest in the collateral. Please confirm whether Mr. Cooper is required to adhere to the provisions of the Uniform Commercial Code, which has been adopted by each state as law. If Mr. Cooper is exempt from these codes, please provide documentation of such an exemption. If Mr. Cooper is obligated to follow the Uniform Commercial Code, please address the following questions : How did Mr. Cooper purchase the note if it was made payable to Nationstar LLC? Has Mr. Cooper received or disbursed any funds or credits in connection with the Promissory Note? If so, why hasnt Mr. Cooper remitted any payments to me or towards the obligation? IRS Tax Standards According to IRS Publication 537, installment sales are to be reported as follows : A bond or other evidence of debt you receive from the buyer thats payable on demand or readily tradable in an established securities market is treated as a payment in the year you receive it. Readily tradable means traded on a registered national securities exchange or a foreign national securities exchange officially recognized by a governmental authority, and the security is deemed by the SEC to have a ready market ( IRC Section 401 ( a ) ( 35 ) ( ii ) ). According to Mr. Coopers SEC filings, my promissory note is actively traded on the open market. Additionally, the note has been converted into a draft, rendering it payable on demand. Consequently, it should have been recorded as a payment to Mr. Cooper. Please answer the following : Is Mr. Cooper exempt from adhering to IRS standards for accounting for Promissory Notes? If so, please provide proof of exemption. If it is not exempt from following IRS standards, please provide me with a reasonable explanation of why the note has not been marked as a payment on its books and the account has not been set to zero? GAAP Accounting Principles As a publicly trading company, Mr. Cooper is required to follow Generally Accepted Accounting Principles ( GAAP ). These principles, established by the Financial Accounting Standards Board ( FASB ), assist in accounting for various financial instruments. According to FASB Statement No. 140, Line 16 : A debtor shall derecognize a liability if and only if it has been extinguished. A liability has been extinguished if either of the following conditions is met : a. The debtor pays the creditor and is relieved of its obligation for the liability. Paying the creditor includes delivery of cash, other financial assets, goods, or services or reacquisition by the debtor of its outstanding debt securities whether the securities are canceled or held as so-called treasury bonds XXXX b. The debtor is legally released from being the primary obligor under the liability, either judicially or by the creditor Financial assets are defined as : cash, evidence of an ownership interest in an entity, or a contract that conveys to one entity a right to receive cash or another financial instrument from a second entity, or to exchange financial instruments on favorable terms with the second entity. Please answer the following questions : Is Mr. Cooper exempt from following the guidelines of G.A.A.P Principles? If so, please provide proof of exemption. Given that my contract is classified as a financial asset, could you please clarify why Mr. Cooper has not extinguished the debt upon the assignment of its rights in the instrument by XXXX XXXX? Following a review of the aforementioned violations, I request that Mr. Cooper promptly address this matter by taking the following action : Utilize the collateral instrument ( note ) to settle the account balance in full and cease any further foreclosure actions. Failure to provide a satisfactory response to all questions and implement the proposed solution will compel me to initiate an audit with the IRS and file a complaint with the SEC. I will also be filing a counterclaim in court and using further evidence to request a judgment for monetary damages and overpayment. I look forward to your prompt resolution of this issue.

I was contacted by Chase Bank by letter that they had determined that my condominium address is in a flood zone, and therefore, I must buy flood insurance to protect their interest in the condo unit. Oddly, they also wrote that FEMA determined my home was in a flood zone. If I did not purchase flood insurance for them, they would do so for me and pass the costs on to me by raising my mortgage. They then wrote that if I believe I'm not in a flood zone, to contact FEMA and to request an amendment or revision to the flood map ( XXXX or XXXX ) and that I would have to pay for any costs associated with getting them to revise the map and send proof. I went to the FEMA website, entered my address and it showed that I was NOT in a flood zone as of XX/XX/year>. So I'm not sure what they are supposed to revise or amend. I called Chase to get more information and the person I spoke to reiterated that FEMA made this determination. I point her to the FEMA website and she said she was not sure how to read the map. She asked me to contact FEMA and to go through the XXXX process. I called FEMA and the person I spoke to said ( 1 ) that FEMA does not communicate with banks about flood map updates, and ( 2 ) Chase bank has a third party they contract with that makes the " Standard Flood Hazard Determinations '' ... or something like that. This XXXX representative then went to their maps and confirmed that my home is not in a flood zone. I asked XXXX what to do and they recommended doing both of the following actions : ( 1 ) Go through the XXXX process but that it takes 60 days ; ( 2 ) File a complaint with the regulatory body over the organization that Chase contracts with to make the determinations, and to contact the state attorney general. FEMA gave me a number to call. I called that number, went through a long menu of option, spoke to someone who then told me that it does sound like Chase is engaged in forced-insurance. She then said the best entity to help me through this is the Consumer Finance Protection Bureau. I decided to contact Chase one more time. I explained the situation, and relayed to them what FEMA said and that FEMA denies communicating with them directly ( contradicting what the previous Chase representative said ). This new Chase rep admits that it was another entity that makes that determination, and reiterated the only remedy available to me is to fill out the XXXX forms at my expense. She also reiterated that if I don't buy a flood insurance policy for Chase, they would do it for me, and pass the costs to me, even though it'll take 2 months before FEMA can send proof that I'm not in a flood zone. She mentioned something about offering a refund if they were wrong, but that seems to contradict aspects of what is written in the letter, particularly where there's a gap in coverage. In short, as best as I understand it, Chase contracts with some 3rd Party to make determinations about whether a property is in a flood zone, then Chase claims that it was FEMA who made that determination, then demands homeowners to buy flood insurance to protect Chase 's interest in the property. If the homeowner doesn't comply, Chase will buy what they openly admit may not be the most affordable insurance. To comply with their demand, they give homeowners LESS than the 60 days it takes to go through the XXXX process ( which you may have to pay for ) to prove you are not in the flood zone, even though ANYONE can simply go to the FEMA website, enter their address, and see that they are not in a flood zone. I did a quick XXXX search and it seems Chase has a history of doing this. This is not at all fair.

My mortgage is a VA loan that was purchased by Newrez a couple of months following its origination. We have had longtime plans to release 1 acre of our 16 acres to our daughter so she can build her home. We got the area surveyed, soil tested, approved by our county committee, and legally separated into its own parcel, but it remains in our name. We had the quitclaim deed written up by legal counsel and took it the county register of deeds to transfer ownership to my daughter. The register of deeds at the county informed us that they are unable to file this quitclaim deed without a partial release from Newrez for this 1 acre out of the 16 acres secured by the lien ( deed of trust ). Upon initiating the process for a partial release, it was discovered that Newrez documents state that only 8 of our 16 acres are being held as collateral because its value was enough according to the appraisal to cover our loan amount should we default. Newrez mortgage documents do NOT match the lien ( deed of trust ) on file with the county, as that document states that newrez is holding all 16 of the acres as collateral. This MAJOR inconsistency in the lien ( deed of trust ) and the mortgage documents was not caught by the underwriter of our loan, the VA officer who approved it, the realtor selling the property, the title company who facilitated this purchase, and Newrez who purchased this loan. Had this been identified by one or more of these parties, I believe the loan would not have closed with this MAJOR error. Upon bringing this error to the partial release team at Newrez, they stated that this is now a legal matter that is to be addressed and corrected by their Legal Remedies team, as the county will not require a partial release when the lien ( deed of trust ) is corrected to state they are holding 8 acres rather then 16 acres. We have contacted this team via email and have not received any response in regard to this matter. This was a legal mistake that was made when the Lien ( deed of trust ) was filed with the county. At this time, the 8 of our 16 acres that Newrez states they are NOT holding as collateral are tied up by Newrez because of the ERROR on the Lien ( deed of trust ). We need this mistake corrected IMMEDIATELY as it is NOT ETHICAL and ILLEGAL for Newrez to be hold 8 acres of our property hostage due to a clerical error that Newrez failed to identify. In the state of Tennessee, this incorrect lien ( deed of trust ) is legally invalid, so it is also in Newrez best interest to correct this immediately as an invalid Lien ( deed of trust ) leaves the loan unsecured. If this is not corrected in a timely manner, we will take legal action to have our 8 acres given back to us.

The TILA protects consumers from unfair or inaccurate credit billing and credit card practices. It also requires lenders to provide loan cost information so that consumers can compare different types of loans. The home does not meet FHA minimum property requirements therefore can not be a level 4. It also states, The purpose of remedies is to mitigate risk to FHA and, if applicable, put Borrowers and/or other affected parties in the position they would have been in absent the violation. When FHA sustains a Tier 1 Finding, Life-of-Loan indemnification is the only remedy available in LRS. Alternatives to indemnification may be available in LRS for Tier 2 Findings. In some cases, multiple remedies may be necessary to address the full impact of an individual Finding. Remedies are described below for unacceptable Findings in LRS. In each defect area, possible remedies for common policy violations are listed in order based on the degree of impact. They are for reference only and may not be all-inclusive of remedies requested by FHA. A. Mitigation Findings may be mitigated in LRS with the Mortgagees submission of one of the following as requested by FHA : additional documentation and/or information that was not included in the original loan file reviewed by FHA, which demonstrates the Mortgagees compliance with HUD policy requirements ; or evidence of corrective actions completed by the Mortgagee which, in FHAs determination, adequately addresses the source and cause of the Finding so that the loan no longer presents an unacceptable risk to FHA. B. Financial Remediation Consistent with FHA rules and requirements, Mortgagees may financially remediate certain loan-level Findings by submitting documentation showing completion of the requested action in the amount specified by FHA. Financial remediation may include : refunds to reimburse unallowable or erroneous charges, fees, or costs to the Borrower; principal reductions applied to the unpaid principal balance of the loan. For delinquent/defaulted loans, funds may be applied to the Borrowers suspense account ; account adjustments to the Borrowers loan, escrow, or suspense account in the amount necessary for the Servicer to bring the account in compliance with HUD policy and/or demonstrate corrective action ; and remittance of improperly paid servicing claims and/or loss mitigation incentives to HUD. text: To whom it may concern, Hello, First, thank you very much for reviewing our complaint. It means a lot to us. We sincerely ask your help to look into their business practices to see if they really postpone the sale date. Or they try to lure customers into believing that the trust sale date can be postponed and keep them from finding another alternatives. 2. This dis Dual Tracking. Me and my wife were trying so hard to keep this house so we sent Mr Cooper Loan Modification Package multiple times so they can modify the loan. On the date they recorded a trust sale date, XX/XX/XXXX, the modification package that we sent on XX/XX/XXXX was still under review. Can they proceed with Trust Sale Date when the Loan Modification Package is under review? Isnt this in violation of dual tracking? ( RESPA 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( g ) ( 2014 ). This prohibited practice proceeding with a foreclosure sale while processing a complete loan modification application submitted at least 37 days before the scheduled sale is known as dual tracking. ) 3. But please find enclosed documents that prove that we had purchase agreement before the sale date and we have opened an escrow. We sincerely ask your help and look into this matter. COMPLAINT I. INTRODUCTION This complaint is filed against BSI Financial Services ( hereinafter Respondent ) for fraudulent, deceptive, and unlawful practices in the execution and servicing of a mortgage loan. Complainant, [ XXXX XXXX ] ( hereinafter Complainant ), asserts that Respondent failed to provide full disclosure regarding the use of Complainants promissory note to generate funds, a violation of federal laws, including the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), as well as fraudulent misrepresentation and breach of contract. This complaint seeks restitution, rescission of the mortgage, and the return of all payments made under the fraudulent mortgage agreement. II. PARTIES Complainant is a resident of [ XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX ] and the mortgage loan borrower under the account number referenced above. Respondent, BSI Financial Services, is a financial institution servicing mortgage loans in [ Maryland ], and is registered to do business in [ Maryland ]. III. JURISDICTION AND VENUE Jurisdiction and venue are appropriate as Respondent is a financial institution operating under federal regulations and servicing loans in this jurisdiction. This complaint arises under federal statutes including the Truth in Lending Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. ) and relevant federal case law. IV. FACTUAL BACKGROUND On or around [ XXXX, XXXX ], Complainant entered into a mortgage agreement with XXXX for the property located at [ XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX ]. Complainant signed a promissory note agreeing to repay the loan over a period of time with interest. Complainant has recently discovered, based on federal banking publications and analysis, that Respondent did not provide actual consideration in this transaction. Specifically, instead of loaning Respondents own money or depositors funds, Respondent used Complainants promissory note to generate the funds for the loan. Complainant was never informed of this practice during the loan process, nor did Respondent disclose this fact in the mortgage contract or associated documents, in violation of federal law and contractual obligations. V. CAUSES OF ACTION COUNT ONE : VIOLATION OF THE TRUTH IN LENDING ACT ( TILA ) ( 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. ) The Truth in Lending Act mandates that lenders provide borrowers with clear and complete disclosure regarding the terms and conditions of loans, including the nature of the financial instruments used to create the loan. Respondent failed to disclose that the loan was funded by the use of Complainants promissory note, a material fact that, if disclosed, would have impacted Complainants decision to enter into the mortgage agreement. The use of Complainants promissory note as an asset violates 15 U.S.C. 1638 ( a ), which requires the lender to fully disclose key loan terms. As a result of this violation, Complainant seeks rescission of the mortgage loan pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1635, along with the restitution of all payments made under the loan, including principal, interest, and associated fees. COUNT TWO : FRAUDULENT MISREPRESENTATION Respondent knowingly failed to disclose material facts concerning the nature of the loan transaction. Specifically, Respondent did not inform Complainant that the loan would be created using Complainants own promissory note as an asset rather than traditional funding from Respondents reserves or depositors. The Supreme Court has ruled that misrepresentation of material facts in contract formation can render the contract voidable. In XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, 126 U.S. 240 ( 1888 ), the Court held that a contract based on fraud or misrepresentation of material facts is unenforceable. Similarly, in United States v. Throckmorton, 98 U.S. 61 ( 1878 ), the Court ruled that contracts induced by fraud are void. By failing to disclose the actual source of the loan funds, Respondent misled Complainant into signing the mortgage contract under false pretenses, thus committing fraud. COUNT XXXXHREE : BREACH OF CONTRACT In a valid contract, both parties must provide consideration. Respondent did not provide valid consideration because it did not loan its own funds or deposits but instead used the Complainants promissory note to create the loan. As established in Restatement ( Second ) of Contracts 71, the absence of consideration renders a contract voidable. The U.S. Supreme Court in XXXX XXXX XXXX, 156 U.S. 680 ( 1895 ) affirmed that contracts lacking proper consideration or founded on fraudulent grounds may be declared invalid. Respondent 's failure to provide consideration and lack of disclosure regarding the use of the promissory note constitutes a breach of contract, entitling Complainant to rescission and restitution. VI. FEDERAL RESERVE PUBLICATIONS SUPPORTING CLAIMS Federal Reserve publications confirm the use of promissory notes by financial institutions to create money, supporting Complainants assertion that Respondent did not loan actual funds. These publications include : Federal Reserve XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX - XXXX XXXX XXXX ( pages 3-4 ) : This document explains how banks create money using borrowers ' promissory notes as assets. The publication explicitly states that banks do not really lend money they create it. Federal Reserve XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX Banking Basics : This document describes the use of promissory notes as money in modern banking systems. Federal Reserve Bank XXXX XXXX XXXX Money, Banking, and Monetary Policy : This publication further explains how promissory notes are utilized by banks to create new funds. These publications establish that Respondent 's use of the promissory note to generate loan funds is a common banking practice, yet Respondent failed to disclose this to Complainant, in violation of federal law.

To Whom It May Concern, I am writing to file a formal complaint against JP Morgan Chase in relation to the handling of my late fathers mortgage. I am doing this not only for my family but in an effort to prevent others from enduring a similar situation. On XX/XX/XXXX, my father unexpectedly passed away, and I discovered that his mortgage was held by Chase. In late XXXX or early XXXX of XXXX, I visited the Chase branch at XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, where I met with an employee named XXXX, who informed me she handles estates for Chase. I explained the complex situation involving my fathers passing, my mothers claim of non-involvement with the mortgage ( per her attorneys advice ), and the fact that my brother and I were handling the estate. XXXX advised me that even if I kept paying the mortgage, once Chase discovered my fathers passing, they would take possession of the house, regardless of whether payments were current. She suggested that I should assume the mortgage to protect my fathers home, claiming that this would give me ownership of the house. She also told me assuming the loan would give me the access I needed to file the home owners insurance claim. This did not seem right to me, as my father intended for my brother and me to share his estate equally. I refused to sign any paperwork and sought legal advice. Multiple attorneys later confirmed that a bank can not legally repossess a home if the mortgage is current, and they reassured me that any such attempt could be legally stopped. For over two years, I paid the mortgage using my fathers information, hoping to resolve matters through probate, which has unfortunately been delayed. In XX/XX/XXXX, I received an escrow surplus check made out to my parents. I visited the same branch and inquired about applying it to the mortgage, as well as the status of the homeowners insurance, which had become more urgent due to worsening conditions in the home. I was told by the mortgage department that I could apply the escrow surplus to the mortgage, but I was later informed that this was incorrect. In XX/XX/XXXX, I learned from the mortgage department that I needed to apply to become the successor of interest to the loan. This was the first time I was told about this process, which caused significant frustration. For over two years, I had lived in fear that Chase might take my fathers home, and I was overwhelmed by the misinformation and stress this caused my family. I applied for and was approved as the successor of interest, but the process was far from straightforward. Throughout this ordeal, I was repeatedly given conflicting information regarding the mortgage, escrow, and homeowners insurance. Additionally, in a conversation with XXXX, I discovered that I had been listed on the homeowners insurance policy all along by my birthdate, along with my brother. This information, which Chase had not disclosed, could have prevented much of the unnecessary stress and worsening home conditions. In XX/XX/XXXX, Chase sent an escrow check to my mother, despite her repeated assertions that she is not responsible for the property. I returned to the branch and was told to provide a letter proving that the funds were mine, only to be met with further delays and miscommunication. When I visited the branch on XX/XX/XXXX, I was met with further condescension and was again provided incorrect information. On XX/XX/XXXX, I spoke with a representative from the mortgage department who informed me that the escrow check could not be reissued in my name, despite previous assurances to the contrary. I was then told that a deceased individual, my late godfather, was responsible for the matter, despite his passing years earlier. At this point, I was advised to hire a lawyer and take the issue to court. For over two years, Chase has misled and misinformed me, causing unnecessary stress and financial hardship for my family. I believe that Chase employed deceptive tactics to coerce me into assuming the mortgage without proper legal guidance. Furthermore, their negligence in handling this matter has led to worsening conditions in the family home and financial strain due to lost work time. I am filing this complaint in hopes that Chase will be held accountable for their actions and to raise awareness of the harm caused to families dealing with the loss of a loved one. I urge you to investigate this matter thoroughly and ensure that no one else endures the same hardships. I also have recordings if needed. My second recording is too big to upload. If you require further information, I can be reached at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX or by email at XXXX. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

Given that the previous year 's homeowners policy was {$2000.00}, and with no other major changes in charges coming out of my escrow account, my monthly mortgage payment should have gone down slightly. However, my XXXX statement indicated that the payment due for XX/XX/XXXX had increased from {$2100.00} to {$2700.00}, an increase of nearly {$700.00}! Throughout the month of XXXX and through to the midpoint of XXXX, I made call after call after call after call. I spoke to well over a dozen people at Truist. Despite my doing all of the work to concel the {$4000.00} renewal with XXXX and replacing it with a {$1700.00} policy with XXXX, Truist didn't mark the {$4000.00} as canceled, no they listed it as an " additional pollicy/wind ''. They also confused my primary homeowners insurance as being an insurance policy as the policy for our guest house. The guest house has a policy on it that expires in XXXX, but somehow, they confused it with the main homeowners policy that expires in XXXX. As such, I was assessed an additional charge of over {$2600.00} as a bank-placed insurance policy for having no insurance at all. This went along with an imaginary " additional insurance/wind of {$4000.00}, AND they also included my XXXX policy for {$1700.00}. That is why my monthly payment increased by {$680.00}. I completely understand that someone could input the wrong figures into the system and that it could spit out the wrong payment amount. However, there is absolutely no excuse for my having to contact Truist a couple dozen times over the course of the summer to get this sorted out. There is no excuse for my calling Truist during normal business hours, ask for a supervisor, and then wait 30 minutes and have the person who answered my call not be able to get a supervisor on the line ( this happened in early XXXX during one of my many calls to Truist ). There is also no excuse for the behaviour of the man ( I didn't catch his name when I called about being given a bank-placed insurance charge of over {$2600.00} for homeowners insurance, but he had a northern style accident, as if he were from someplace like Minnesota or XXXX ) who upon my explaining that I did in fact have insurance that Truist paid it out of my escrow account, received a XXXX page for it, had specifically confirmed they had it, AND had it updated upon my login to the online banking site, actually had the audacity to tell me that the CFPB mandated Truist sending that letter to me and having a policy of forcing Truist to send those disclosures. I told him that he should actually read the laws he was spouting off to me and update his understanding, because bank-placed insurance ( and the disclosures that go with it ) are for accounts that don't have mandated insurance policies in place. I told him my account is fully insured, has never lapsed, and Truist has acknowledged this, but falsely sent me the bill for $ XXXX. Despite all this, he again, very condescendingly I might add, completely ignored what I said and then repeated that CFPB mandated Truist sending me that bill. When I told him he was basically out of his mind, wasn't listening, and was being a condescending XXXX who needed to actually read the laws he was spouting off on, then demanded that I speak to a supervisor, he simply hung up on me. I acknowledge that it isn't nice to call someone an XXXX, but by this point I'd had it with with Truist and the months of endless headaches from endless incompetence. And it wasn't like this was the end of it! This was right around the XXXX of XXXX. I still had to call over and over and over again. In the end I spoke to more than a dozen more people! They all acknowledged all of mistakes I've described here. They acknowledged that the {$4000.00} policy renewal should not have ever been paid in the first place, and that it should never have been also clasified on my account as an " additional policy/wind ''. They acknowledged that my XXXX policy for {$1700.00} satisfied my policy requirements and should not have been tied to my guest house policy. And they certainly acknowledged that I should have never have been charged with bank-placed insurance for over {$2600.00}! But in the end it was 2 representatives I spoke to, XXXX and XXXX, who listened to my seeming endless tale of incompetence, said they would do something, and then called me back and communicated with me as they shepherded the process along and got my issue fixed and my payment finally corrected on the XXXX of XXXX ( my payment is now corrected to {$2000.00} ). Despite my issue being resolved, the incredible incompetence of Truist can not be understated. They screwed up over and over again. They didn't listen over and over and over again.
