Dear CFPB : I am writing to file a formal complaint against Guaranteed Rate Affinity regarding their handling of my mortgage application process for the purchase of a condominium at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, NY. The issues I have experienced relate to predatory lending practices, failure to disclose substantial fees, and the refusal to provide a decline letter, which has caused me significant financial loss. I applied for a loan with Guaranteed Rate Affinity after being declined by XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX. I was approved for a mortgage with an initial loan estimate of approximately {$88000.00}. However, just two days before closing, I was presented with a final loan estimate that was more than {$10000.00} higher than the initial estimate. This increase was unexpected, and I did not have sufficient funds to cover the additional amount. Upon consulting with my attorney, we realized that additional fees, including legal fees, had not been disclosed, further exacerbating the issue. I informed Guaranteed Rate Affinity of my financial situation and my inability to proceed. However, instead of declining my loan due to insufficient funds ( which would have allowed me to terminate my contract with the condo seller without penalty ), they pressured me to voluntarily withdraw my loan application. I believe this practice is unfair and caused me to forfeit 50 % of my down payment, as I was unable to secure the decline letter, which was a stipulation in the contract with the seller. I never contacted Guaranteed Rate Affinity to voluntarily withdraw from the loan application, and I would like to know what reasoning they had in asking me to withdraw, rather than reaching out to my lawyer, who should have handled such a critical decision. I feel it is predatory to pressure a borrower into withdrawing from a loan application without allowing proper time for consultation, and I believe Guaranteed Rate Affinity was well aware of the potential harm this could cause. Additionally, I find it concerning that, despite the closing being set for XX/XX/XXXX, I received a call on XX/XX/XXXX from XXXX XXXX, asking if I would like to withdraw my loan application. This call was made while my attorney was on vacation, and no efforts were made to explore all possible options. I question the timing and motives behind this call and the pressure placed on me to withdraw without representation. Moreover, I believe Guaranteed Rate Affinity engaged in predatory lending practices by suggesting that I find additional funds or sell assets to complete the purchase. I was led into a financially precarious situation without being fully informed of all the fees and potential liabilities, which I believe violates consumer protection laws. I am requesting the following actions : An investigation into the lending practices of Guaranteed Rate Affinity related to my mortgage application. A determination of whether Guaranteed Rate Affinitys failure to provide a decline letter and their pressure for me to withdraw my application constitutes a violation of federal lending laws. Compensation for the financial losses I have incurred due to these actions, including the loss of 50 % of my down payment and any associated legal fees. I have attached documentation related to my mortgage application, loan estimates, and communications with Guaranteed Rate Affinity. Please feel free to contact me for any additional information or clarification. Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your prompt investigation and resolution of my complaint. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

They did so and my credit score has returned to the XXXX level. Several months earlier, FM also gave me back my online access so I could view my account statements. Today I learned, they refuse to provide me with any information regarding my own account over the phone, by email, or through their website - an account for which I make 100 % of the payments. Our trustee gave Wells Fargo to submit all documents necessary and amount or arrearage to her by XX/XX/XXXX. Unfortunately Wells Fargo lagged and missed the court date. On XX/XX/XXXX according to my attorney XXXX XXXX Wells Fargo contacted the bankruptcy court and asked if our attorney would make a motion to reopen the case so the arrearage could be rolled into the chapter XXXX unfortunately it would cost more money to reopen my case. Our Trustee XXXX XXXX XXXX agreed upon the motion to reopen the case for Wells Fargo so long as they would modify our loan. We have tried two prior occasions once last XX/XX/XXXX and the second time XX/XX/XXXX. Those two occasions were turned down from modification. Since the case was resubmitted in XX/XX/XXXX we were denied two more times and we were notified by our home preservation specialist at Wells Fargo XXXX XXXX that we could appeal the decision by rewriting another letter of hardship and they would review the case again. When we told her that our Trustee could possibly retract on the arrearage and not included in the XXXX XXXX payments because they had not followed through with their agreement, she was told that they would begin following procedure to repossess our home. We were mailed a letter stating that our hardship was not permanent nor it was enough to modify our loan. We explained to XXXX, if we were not in a hardship, our payments would be current. XXXX also informed her that in order to modify alone you must be current on your home payments. However, at this point we were two more payments behind due to our hardship. We explained to XXXX XXXX if we could make our payments we would not be needing a modification. As of XX/XX/XXXX we appealed our case again and we were sent a letter stating that Wells Fargo would re-review our case. Within a week, my wife made a formal complaint against Wells Fargo practices to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, Attorney General of Texas XXXX XXXX, The US Justice Department, and Consumer Federal Protection Bureau. My wife was given a call by XXXX XXXX XXXX an executive mortgage specialist. She informed my wife once again we did not qualify for the modification because our income to payment ratio was not enough. The percent they got made it look like we could afford our home. They based it on our gross income. That does not help anybody to qualify. As there are overhead expenses and taxes to take into consideration. That makes no sense at all. XXXX XXXX informed my wife that there were no other programs to save us from losing our home except for a short sale. My wife informed her that we didnt want to lose our home and asked how it would be possible to qualify for a modification loan. XXXX XXXX told my wife if she was to close down her business then we would qualify. That means I would have to make absolutely no income and be on time on my payments. That was not an answer. We expected to hear from a person who is an executive mortgage specialist for Wells Fargo not a bully. We felt attacked and helpless at this point. How can anyone doing this have a conscience. On XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX sent a letter with her version of how we were at fault for why Wells Fargo would not modify us. She mentioned in the letter that as of XX/XX/XXXX it was determined that we were unable to approve a workout option for the loan. She also mentioned that the criteria that needed to be met, which would need to include the inability to maintain payments on the property as a result of a financial hardship. So one minute Im being told I have to be current on my loan to qualify, but now its being said that we would have to have the inability to maintain payments on the property as a result of a financial hardship to qualify. At the end of the letter, one of the last lines on page XXXX says as of the date of this correspondence, the mortgage loan is contractually due for the XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX mortgage installments. What does that mean? We were in arrearage 10 months. Wouldnt that qualify me for a modification loan based on what XXXX XXXX states in the letter directed to myself, my lawyer, XXXX XXXX XXXX, and the CFPB. Obviously, even after she sent this letter, it was proven that there was a way for me to get modified for some sort of modification loan. XXXX XXXX through Wells Fargo. My wife told XXXX XXXX that we would no longer be making our mortgage payments if she was going to assume the process of repossessing our home. My wife had also read up on an article that Wells Fargo was involved in a discrimination case against Latin Americans and African-Americans between XXXX that was settled in XX/XX/XXXX. After researching this case we are beginning to feel discriminated against. My wife and I at that point stopped making our payments to Wells Fargo because we felt that if we were not going to be modified this time, they would take our home from us anyway. We were emotionally exhausted with the mirage that they cared and wanted to help their customers. We do not rely on anyone to bail out just to be fair. All we asked was fairness from the bank that had a huge bail out from the government. Because of Wells Fargo we were forced to file for bankruptcy so we could have some thing to protect us from losing our home and there was no way we could catch up on 10 months of payments. What I found interesting was once I made my formal complaint to our US Senator all of the sudden I was able to get modified and they were able to help me. I also find it disheartening how I was told we didnt qualify and there was nothing Wells Fargo could do to help. My automatic assumption is that Wells Fargo just wanted to take my home anyway. It caused so much hardship and heartache trying to have to explain to our children at that time that we were going to be homeless and that the bank was going to take our home. The persistent callers, visits, and mail we received from the threat to reposes our home from Wells Fargo was excruciating. I believe their hope was that they could posses my home before the trustee would give them an opportunity to reopen the case. At this point our credit was ruined, we had to wait five years to finish our XXXX XXXX, which we paid off, and 10 years for it to come off of our record which put us in XXXX just last year. During this time we were unable to help our son with college, purchase a vehicle because one of our vehicles had been totaled, nearly divorced as to break up our family, and dealt with severe XXXX. When we received your letter of mediation. I decided to go ahead, and follow through with it because I feel like I was not treated fairly and we were not taken care of by Wells Fargo. Whether it is discrimination or just the fact that Wells Fargo is so greedy, they didnt care who they took their homes from. They gladly accepted the bail out from the government and didnt use any of that money to help modify the people who needed it the most. We are middle class hard working people and we dont rely on the government unless necessary. Thankfully we have been able to come out of this, but not without the pain and suffering it caused. I believe Wells Fargo should be responsible for at the very least a settlement which we would be happy to negotiate. In the meantime, I have already contacted our US Senator once again, and the CFPB I have let them know up to this point nothing has been resolved regarding mediation. We are waiting for the Senator to reply and CFPB to respond. I will also be attaching all of the hardship letters that I sent to Wells Fargo, to the CFPB, president of Wells Fargo, and to the office of XXXX XXXX XXXX during the process.

A few months ago, a hail storm hit our area and the area was designated as a disaster area. I soon received a document that said I was auto-approved and my account was put into forbearance. I didnt have enough information about what it meant for me to even approve this is what I needed or wanted. Freedom Mortgage pushed me into forbearance without full disclosure or agreement. Also, my account was placed under a Loss Mitigation status, which is collections or delinquent. I received a call today from a collections agent that had no idea why he was calling me. My account is fully paid each month and never late. The agent opened the call saying that I was due for the XXXX payment. Its not even due yet. The agent could not explain to me why they auto approved a forbearance nor could he explain why Freedom Mortgage told me that I dont have to make any payments until the forbearance period ends. The agent was focused on collecting a payment for something that wasnt due. It felt like the agent was just calling to tell me my account status was in loss mitigation and I had a payment due, which is unfair to me and deceptive. The practice of auto approving the forbearance without fully disclosing and educating me on what that means seems like an abusive policy. If I were to have followed Freedom Mortgages direction and not made my payments, I would have been significantly behind and could have lost my home. Im very confused and frustrated. I dont think as a XXXX combat veteran that Freedom Mortgage had my best interest in its forbearance process/policy.

I called my mortgage company requesting instructions for removing the escrow. I have owned homes previously without an escrow requirement and have always paid property taxes and insurance as required. The escrow requirement was put in place because we put a down payment on our current home of less than 20 %. However, we bought the home at a below market price, and once our previous home sold, put over {$150000.00} in cash into the current home for improvements. When I requested removal of the escrow, the mortgage company cited RESPA guidelines stating that my mortgage balance must be less than 80 % of the original purchase price of the home. Considering the money we put into the home and my past history of paying taxes and insurance in a timely fashion, I feel this is highly unreasonable. I am willing to have the property re-assessed at my expense in order to validate that the balance is now well below the 80 % threshold, but the RESPA guidelines do not allow that. These guidelines need to be amended for people who have worked hard to put money into their homes to enhance the value and no longer wish to be subject to escrow requirements.

On XX/XX/year>, FBC indicated a discrepancy between the lease and tax returns rental income and area market rental income and did not respond to requests to describe the disparity in mathematical terms. 4. text: Hello, I am writing this letter to help explain my situation in further detail, hoping you understand this tough time. My husband, our kids, and I were blessed with the opportunity to build this home in XXXX, Texas, from the ground up. We really enjoyed watching this process. Our toddler boys also had much excitement throughout this journey as well. We closed on XX/XX/XXXX. I was working off the road then but was planning to return to the local area to enjoy this beautiful home we had built. After closing, at the end of XX/XX/XXXXXXXX XXXX my husband was involved in an accident with an XXXX and three other vehicles. It was the scare of our lives at an extremely rough time ; we had just closed one month ago. We had not had time to get ourselves recouped financially with such unpredictable circumstances at hand. I was forced to come off the road earlier than expected, which involved a pay decrease. I kept the mortgage payments current for a few months before finances got tight. My husband immediately sought legal action since the XXXX that caused this accident had fled the scene leaving four innocent citizens stranded without any concern. Due to the physical bodily trauma that my husband was left to recover from, he was legally advised to take a leave from work. His attorney began working on this case immediately. My husband was medically released to go back to work in XX/XX/XXXX. Being the sole provider of the household during this time, with a brand-new mortgage, caused us to fall into this hardship. I was praying that once the case was settled, the settlement disbursement would be just enough to catch us back up and help us become current on our mortgage. I couldn't care less about having any extra funds to save. I was only concerned with catching up on our mortgage. Unfortunately, it was not enough. The disbursement was released in XX/XX/XXXX and was only a small fraction of the arrears. Being that this was our first home purchased, I was unfamiliar with the options I could juggle at this time. However, I did seek advice from a few trusted individuals. I was given information about the Texas Homeowner Assistance program. In XX/XX/XXXX, I filed an application with the Texas Homeowner Assistance program and received notice in XXXX that our application had been denied due to income limitations in XXXX XXXX. After being 120 days past due on the mortgage in XXXX, I spoke with the bank and learned about loss mitigation. One thing I can take away from this entire journey is the amount of information I have learned about home ownership. I would have completed the loss mitigation paperwork sooner had I known. I take responsibility for not contacting XXXX as much as I should have. I just felt as if this situation was going to turn around somehow. I completed the loss mitigation paperwork in XXXX but was denied due to income. At this time, I saved more than 50 % of the arrears amount but was denied the ability to pay it since it was all or nothing. The demand letter was sent and the very first auction date was approaching. I knew my back was against the wall. Unfortunately, at this point, we were forced to file for bankruptcy. I could not fathom losing what was supposed to be our forever home at this time. My husband was making every effort to get back to work during this time ; however, the physical restrictions he was dealing with from the accident became an issue with several jobs he attained. After surrendering three jobs due to his condition, he decided to do small projects on the side to contribute to our income. Still, it was not enough to even keep up the bankruptcy payments, and I was working as much as possible. The bankruptcy was dismissed in XXXX due to income and a tax error that we could not fix by the court ruling date. I knew this meant we were back in the pre-foreclosure process, and we still have not been able to catch up on finances. I had no idea we would be facing foreclosure and losing our home. It is a hard realization to process. I have learned some hard lessons throughout this process, but I am still thankful for the knowledge and humility it has left us with. I know that we will make better decisions the next time we purchase and be more prepared. In short, I fell behind in XX/XX/XXXX due to the hardship of having only one income to support the household while having a decline in my income as well. I have attempted to rectify the default by applying for a loan modification, for which I was also denied due to my income. I am now in the process of applying for a short sale in an attempt to avoid foreclosure. Please postpone the upcoming auction date by 90 days to allow time for me to complete the short sale process. I want to make this right and do my due diligence to XXXX as best I can. I ask that you grace me with this opportunity. Thank you so much for your time and consideration. Genuinely, A customer

Hello, I am writing about a particular issue relating to home insurance, and what I believe to be an unfair practice by my mortgage provider, Wells Fargo. I'm a longtime customer of Wells Fargo. I am current on my loan and do not need assistance. I have never missed a payment ; I have never been late with a payment. ( In fact, this is my second loan with the company in two decades. ) The problem relates to how I pay for home insurance. I typically pay for a year of coverage up front, separate from my mortgage payments. In XX/XX/XXXX, I inadvertently missed the renewal for my original home insurer, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX didn't contact me to ensure I would renew. Nevertheless, this was my mistake. But I wasn't aware of the mistake until XX/XX/XXXX, when I received notice by mail from Wells Fargo that my mortgage was without insurance, and that this was against the rules. I immediately bought new coverage ( from XXXX XXXX ) and uploaded that information. However, because of the inadvertent lapse in coverage, Wells Fargo is charging me for expensive insurance retroactively for a period of time that's already months past. I've notified Wells Fargo and it says the fact that XXXX didn't provide notice isn't its problem. In addition, it's going to charge me for insurance for the period where I didn't have coverage. In other words, too bad. I believe that insurance works to cover potential claims in the future ; it doesn't work retroactively. ( One doesn't get into an accident today, and then buy car insurance tomorrow. ) Also, I think that having mortgage lenders impose premiums at will creates opportunities for abuse. Finally, it's troubling to me that roughly a year went by before anyone reached out. Once I was notified of a problem, I rectified my mistake immediately. Therefore, I am formally submitting this as a qualified written request. Upon review, it appears that my current Loan-to-Value ( LTV ) ratio is cited as 94.6 %. However, there is no stipulation within my original loan agreement that mandates an escrow account solely based on the LTV ratio. Additionally, the loan documents provide that the escrow account can be canceled upon request, provided certain conditions are met. I have met all other conditions outlined in your letter, and the LTV ratio alone should not be a disqualifying factor, especially since it was not explicitly required in the loan terms. Furthermore, the terms of my loan agreement do not specify that the maintenance of an escrow account is compulsory if my LTV exceeds a certain percentage. Given this, I request that the escrow account be canceled as per my initial request. Please treat this correspondence as a formal and qualified written request under RESPA. I urge you to reconsider your position and proceed with the cancellation of my escrow account. If my impounds are not removed, I will have no choice but to file a formal complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) and any other relevant regulatory bodies. I appreciate your prompt attention to this matter and look forward to your favorable response.

We were struggling with a lot of credit card debt and had decided against the personal loan route because of interest rates in the double digits when we received a mailing from our current primary mortgage lender, Freedom Mortgage, alerting us to the potential of additional equity in the house that we could borrow against. We already had a home equity loan from a few years back when we renovated the entire basement so I wasn't sure of the options but decided to at least inquire. I received a call from XXXX XXXX that same day, XX/XX/XXXX ; he said we would have to refinance the entire primary mortgage and pay off the home equity loan/ second mortgage along with our credit cards, it would be a 5.75 % interest rate, and the only choice he gave me was between our existing term of 22 years and a new term of 30 years. I made it very clear that I am a person who likes all the information and told him I had to take the day to ponder and crunch numbers because we would be giving up a 3 % interest rate on our primary mortgage. After discussing in great detail and going over our existing monthly payments versus what our new budget would look like we did decide to move forward because we would in turn also be paying off our credit cards which have interest rates between 23 and 29 %. I called him back the next day, and confirmed we did want to proceed, at which point he re-stated the interest rate of 5.75 % and said that it was now locked. A few weeks later, when reviewing the Loan Estimate worksheet I questioned a few things : the XXXX re-inspection fee being listed as {$300.00} when the VA fee schedule shows a XXXX of {$150.00}, the {$400.00} we had to prepay for the appraisal not being reflected, as well as what they called 'Origination Charges ' being 4.9 % as I knew that what the XXXX XXXX XXXX ' fees are maxed at 1 % for VA loans XXXX XXXX said the numbers on this worksheet were just placeholders and the final closing worksheet would be the final and correct numbers, and as far as the Origination Charges ' being 4.9 % he gave me the reasoning " that the 1 % cap is only for new purchases and not for cash-out ''. We did e-sign it because he insisted it was ( just like everything else ) 'time sensitive ' and needed to be signed immediately to prevent delays in the processing of the loan, but I still wanted to confirm with a VA contact since I could not find that differentiation in my research, so I found an online resource where I could ask general questions, and sent them an email. We were able to get the required repairs from the appraisal completed and for the appraiser to come back out within the week which moved our loan through underwriting and to get scheduled for closing before I received any responses to my email. The next morning I received a response from a VA representative stating 'the maximum origination fee for a purchase or cash-out is 1 % of the loan amount ' so I immediately contacted Freedom Mortgage to speak with someone to try and clarify the different information I was being given. I was transferred to the closing department where I spoke with a representative who said the 'origination fee ' is just the 'points ' we are paying to get a lower interest rate, which I was very confused about since I was only given one interest rate the entire time. She then said she couldn't give me any other information since she wasn't licensed and I had to speak with the loan officer. I was obviously uncomfortable considering at this point he had essentially misled me at least twice, but she said we had to speak with the designated loan officer and could or would not provide the name of a supervisor. When I spoke with XXXX his response was " most borrowers don't want to hear about a higher interest rate '' and his apology was " I'm sorry I didn't discuss that with you and just went the route most borrowers want to go, the lower interest rate ''. I asked how it didn't also come up when I specifically asked about that line item and he simply repeated " like I said I do apologize '' but it didn't feel sincere. This wasn't a simple oversight ; it was intentional lack of disclosure. Otherwise, when I inquired about it he would have been the one to tell me those were points to buy down our interest rate, if he had honestly forgotten to mention it the first time, and he wouldn't have fabricated some story about the reasoning being the type of financing we were pursuing or insisted that " most borrowers don't want to hear about a higher interest rate '' if this wasn't his intention all along. For XXXX to insist he is doing his customers a favor by only disclosing the lower interest rate without discussing what you have to pay in exchange is ridiculous. On the contrary, showing borrowers all of the information up front and exploring the option to lower that in exchange for points with them would allow the loan officer the opportunity to show them potential savings over the life of the loan, and if they choose to go that route, would make them feel better about the lower rate. For them to only present the most advantageous route for their company, to receive one lump payment rather than wait several years for the interest to trickle in, without knowing or exploring with the borrower their plans, such as how long they plan to stay in the home, if they are planning a refinance before the break-even point, etc. is an unfair trade practice. For some borrowers several extra XXXX dollars at the time of closing to go towards debit with higher interest rates may outweigh the savings of getting to the break-even point. Not to mention the fact that I had to do my own research to find the information to even weigh the options ; borrowers should be better informed and be given the opportunity to make an educated decision and for everyone to be on the same page from day one to avoid feeling yanked around and/or taken advantage of. In addition to that, some borrowers may be shopping around for rates, and it could be the critical difference in deciding which company to go with. We had to pay out of pocket for half of the appraisal up front, which says on the cover page that it is prepared specifically for this company, so we feel like we have to continue moving forward with them and not waste the money to redo that part again for another company, but it is very upsetting to think that by doing business with them we may be condoning their behavior. Lastly, while I know the disclosure of 'this call may be recorded ' every time you call doesn't guarantee there is a recording, I hope Freedom Mortgage will at least check and properly investigate this claim rather than allowing their loan officers to decide the structure of a proposed loan and ignoring their ethical obligation of full disclosure to their clients.

In early XXXX XX/XX/XXXX, I applied for temporary Hardship Assistance with Freedom Mortgage after losing my job in XX/XX/XXXX. My intention was to pause payments or seek deferment while I navigated a competitive job market. Unfortunately, the lack of clear communication throughout the process resulted in significant damage to my credit and caused confusion regarding the terms and implications of applying for hardship assistance. During the application process, there was no information provided about the potential impact on my credit score. No mention of this was included in the application, nor was I informed whether payments needed to be made during the review process. The only communication I received was an email requesting additional documentation, which I provided promptly. Throughout the review period, I reached out to Freedom Mortgage several times, including a recorded call on XX/XX/XXXX. During this initial call, I was reassured that payments were not required during the hardship review process, as the purpose of such assistance was to offer relief during financial hardship. I received no additional email or correspondence outlining the potential consequences of non-payment during this period. It wasnt until after I was reported delinquent and contacted Freedom Mortgage myself that I was informed of the impact on my credit score. By that time, the damage had been done, and my credit score had dropped from XXXX to XXXX, a XXXX decrease. I dont recall receiving any prior notifications via email or mail, and if any important details about credit impact were buried in paper correspondence, they were easily missed. After nearly XXXX months of waiting, I was finally presented with a forbearance option that allowed me to defer payments until XX/XX/XXXX, at which point the entire past-due balance would be duea solution that offered no real relief given my circumstances. BASIS OF MY COMPLAINT : Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) Violations : Under the FCRA ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ), Freedom Mortgage is obligated to provide accurate information to credit bureaus and to properly notify borrowers about the implications of missed payments. I was not adequately informed of the impact on my credit before it was reported, and the communication only came after the delinquency had already been reported. This constitutes a failure to provide timely and clear information, violating FCRAs obligations for fair and accurate credit reporting. Negligent Misrepresentation : During my conversations with Freedom Mortgage representatives, I was assured that payments were not required while my application was under review. This assurance was misleading and resulted in financial harm. According to Illinois law ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ), negligent misrepresentation occurs when false or incomplete information is provided in the course of business and leads to economic harm, which is exactly what happened in my case. I acted based on Freedom Mortgages misinformation, causing my credit to suffer. Failure to Inform Under the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ) : Under RESPA ( 12 U.S.C. 2605 ), mortgage servicers are required to communicate clearly and promptly with borrowers about their loans. Freedom Mortgages failure to provide me with timely information regarding the consequences of non-payment and their failure to properly inform me about the status of my hardship application for nearly XXXX months demonstrates a breach of this duty. This lack of communication directly contributed to the damage to my credit. Citations : -FCRA ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ) : Governs the accuracy of credit reporting by mortgage lenders. -Negligent Misrepresentation ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, XXXX ) : Legal precedent regarding misrepresentation of information in business that causes economic harm. -RESPA ( 12 U.S.C . 2605 ) : Federal law mandating timely and clear communication from mortgage servicers.

Instead of providing the requested information, Dovenmuehle responded by merely sending a copy of my mortgage documents, which did not address or include the chain of title as requested. Robo-signing, the practice of signing mortgage documents without proper review or authority, is illegal because it violates legal requirements for due diligence, accuracy, and verification in legal documentation. Key laws and regulations that protect against robo-signing include the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX Act, which established the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) to oversee and enforce fair lending practices. MrCooper charged a fee that is not in the mortgage agreement and has a fee disclosure on periodic statements that violates XXXX. My bank made a clerical error and sent a check to MrCooper. The bank canceled the check due to the clerical error. When MrCooper received the check they charged me a {$50.00} " returned payment fee. '' A payment for the correct amount was sent prior to the due date. At no time was my account past due. The periodic statements indicate that MrCooper may charge a fee " up to {$50.00}, '' the right to charge a returned payment fee is not in any of my mortgage documents. Additionally, the " up to '' language on the statement is a clear violation of XXXX as there is no way to pay less than {$50.00} as this is the first fee ever charged on this account. The charging of the fee meets the test for multiple UDAAP prongs : Deceptive : I. The act or practice must cause or be likely to cause substantial injury to consumers. The charge of {$50.00} to me and other customers is substantial. II. The consumers interpretation of the representation is reasonable under the circumstances. - Customers reasonable expect to only be charged fees agreed to in their mortgage documents. Additionally, customers expect when they see the language " up to '' that there are situations where a lower fee will be charged. III. The misleading representation is material. - I and other customers relied on the mortgage agreement to assume that only fees we agreed to would be charged. Additionally, Myself and other customers would be more careful and try to find alternative solutions if we realized that we would be charged the max fee on the first instance. Abusive : I. The act or practice materially interferes with the ability of a consumer to understand a term or condition of a consumer financial product or service. - A fee was charged that was not in the agreement. The " up to '' language made any potential fees seem more reasonable. II. The act or practice takes unreasonable advantage of the inability of the consumer to protect the interests of the consumer in selecting or using a consumer financial product or service. - Customers have no choice in selecting their loan servicers. As such MrCooper is arbitrarily charging customers fees that are not in their mortgage agreement and do not provide customers with a way to pay less than {$50.00} despite saying they charge " up to {$50.00} ''

I am writing to formally lodge a complaint regarding a wrongful foreclosure and the subsequent unlawful eviction attempt by Freedom Mortgage Corporation. Despite my filing for XXXX XXXX bankruptcy, a sheriff 's sale proceeded, during which Freedom Mortgage sold the property to themselves. They have evicted me from my home. Below, I outline the details of my situation and the violations committed. Background : I purchased my property on XX/XX/XXXX. By XX/XX/XXXX, my mortgage had been transferred to three different lenders, raising significant concerns. Within just 24 days of Freedom Mortgage assuming the role of lender, my FHA 30-year fixed mortgage payment was inexplicably increased. On XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX, I submitted affidavits requesting confirmation that Freedom Mortgage held the promissory note, had the authority to enforce it, and asking for debt validation as required under the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ) and the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ). I also requested full accounting documentation in accordance with 15 U.S.C. 44, as outlined in IRS Publication 583. My requests were consistently ignored, in clear violation of federal law. Despite this, a year later, Freedom Mortgage initiated foreclosure proceedings, blatantly disregarding both state and federal laws and my consumer rights. No promissory note was ever presented, and all requests for disclosures regarding account information were ignored. Key Issues : 1. Failure to Validate Debt : Despite repeated requests, Freedom Mortgage failed to provide validation of the debt, including the promissory note, in violation of TILA, RESPA, and other consumer protection laws. Would not respond to billing error also mentioned in affidavit as well as request for disclosures and other documentation. 2. Improper Assignment Involving MERS : Freedom Mortgage began collecting payments in XX/XX/XXXX but did not have an assignment until XX/XX/XXXX. MERS acted as the assignor, though legally, MERS can not assign a mortgage if it does not hold the note, nor does it have the authority to act beyond its role as a recorder ( MERS v. XXXX, XXXX ; In re XXXX, XXXX ). The corporate assignment document incorrectly lists MERS as a nominee for XXXX XXXX XXXX, which XXXX no longer held the note or mortgage at the time. This recorded documentation makes no clear mention of the holder of note or mortgage at the time of this assignment. The document falsely claims I executed it, which I did not and had no knowledge of it raising serious concerns about its legitimacy. 3. Failure to Present Promissory Note : Freedom Mortgage never presented the promissory note, despite my requests and its necessity for legal foreclosure ( Restatement ( Third ) of Property ( Mortgages ), Section 5.4 ). The last known promissory note was endorsed by XXXX XXXX, the only entity legally authorized to transfer or assign it. This raises questions about the validity of Freedom Mortgages corporate assignment and their standing to foreclose, suggesting potential violations including fraudulent assignment, breach of contract, clouded title ( Indiana Code 32-21-4-1 ), FDCPA violations ( 15 U.S.C. 1692e ), and consumer fraud ( IC 24-5-0.5 ). 4. Improper Sale of Property : Freedom Mortgage sold the property to themselves at the sheriff sale, potentially violating Financial Accounting Standards Board ( FASB ) rules, specifically ASC 860 - Transfers and Servicing. True Sale Requirement : For a transaction to be treated as a sale ( and for the assets to be removed from the sellers balance sheet ), it must be a true sale, meaning the seller must relinquish control of the assets. Arms Length Transaction : The sale must be to an unrelated party in an arms length transaction. This transaction raises questions about whether the original sale was legitimate and properly accounted for. 5. Lack of Disclosure Regarding Securitization : Due to the lack of disclosure, I am uncertain whether securitization occurred. Freedom Mortgage 's partnership with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, CIK # XXXX XXXX # XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX IRS NO : XXXX further complicates this issue. If securitization did take place, it would exacerbate the existing legal violations.

text: Slightly over a year ago ( XX/XX/XXXX ), Chase Bank ( who holds my mortgage ) lowered my monthly payment. ( From {$1400.00} to {$1100.00} ) When I questioned it, I was told there was too much money in my escrow account. Beginning this month ( XX/XX/XXXX ) Chase has refigured my monthly payment and is now asking for {$2600.00} ) When I questioned this, they informed me that my escrow account was behind by over {$8000.00}. ( This number has now risen to more than {$10000.00}. ) When I asked what the issue was, I was initially told that I had failed in my responsibility to question XXXX XXXX regarding an incorrect tax bill. Further investigation revealed that this incorrect tax bill had nothing to do with my or my account. It is not the PIN associated with my property and it is not now nor has it ever been associated with my name. Chase attached this PIN to my account and evidently used this information for the refiguring of the mortgage in XXXX of XXXX. When asked how I could have been aware of this error, as XXXX XXXX would not have informed me of information regarding an account that did not belong to me in any way, Chase still insisted that I should somehow have known because my payment was not enough to cover my own taxes. ( Please note that I did check and my taxes had been paid. Also, the balance in my escrow account always shows {$0.00}. I have asked about this and the explanation seems to be that it's how it is done. ) Chase has now realized their own error and wishes to recoup their outlay of funds. ( The person I worked with was insistent that escrow accounts are a " service they offer but that Chase can not take responsibility for them. '' However it is not an optional service and I am required to participate. The purpose of an escrow account is to pay taxes and insurance, and Chase was liable to cover those bills as they came due. If I had been informed at any time that the account was falling in arrears, I would have made arrangements to change the payment structure, but I was not allowed to do so. On XX/XX/XXXX after XXXX phone calls ( during which Chase admitted to the error with the incorrect PIN that caused the issue with the payment being lowered ), I visited a local branch in person to get to the bottom of the issue. During the time that the escrow account is said to be in arrears, Chase claims to have issued a refund of money in the account ( {$5100.00} ). However I never received the money. After six months, the money was refunded to the account after six months because no one cashed the check ( that I did not receive ). Chase now claims that the account was in arrears already when they lowered the payment and issued the refund. This seems to hinge on the PIN that they incorrectly associated with my account. They are unwilling to offer extended time to pay the money Chase paid toward my taxes, insisting that in spite of their error, I should have known that they made a mistake and have the money easily available. They have repeatedly told me that although they acknowledge their error, it is still my responsibility to have known. At the in person meeting, Chase agreed to review my escrow account and to rush the process. They have not done so. They said the process would take a week. It has been two. They also suggested that I not pay my XXXX mortgage until this is resolved, assuring me that it isn't actually late until XX/XX/XXXX. They refused my request to put this in writing multiple times saying that they could not offer this advice except verbally. Chase has not offered any assistance in resolving this situation regardless of being informed that their new calculation places my monthly mortgage out of my price range on a teacher 's salary. They have told me that I do not have to use their " free and helpful '' service to maintain an escrow account but admit that the escrow is mandatory. Evidently there is a way to opt out of escrow if I have met certain criteria, but although they offered to share that criteria, they have not. It should be noted that there is no evidence that Chase paid the tax bill that they attached to my account incorrectly. So if they believed that I owed that amount, they have failed in their primary legal role as a mortgage company. When I asked about this, I was informed that they can not share information on that bill because I am not associated with the PIN.

Our family decided to build a house and the builder suggested we use XXXX from Huntington. During the initial meeting in XXXX with Huntington Representative, XXXX, we discussed our desire to waive escrow, it was made to seem like it would not be a problem. We discussed the nature of our income and that we receiveregular bolus payments and in an effort to bring our monthly payment down we would like to waive escrowand make the property tax payments and insurance payments.This was made to seem like it would be no problem. Hearing this we thought we had everything we wanted and the numbers made sense and we felt totally comfortable. Our initial loan disclosurescame in XXXX and did include escrow, this was explained to be just a rough draft and will change as the process goes on. Since this mortgage would be for a new build we were then offered the option to lock in our interest rate and asked we make a Rate Lock Deposit payment of {$5900.00}, which we did in XXXX. This was sold to us as a protective measure over the changing interest rate. With zero communication from XXXX between the months of XXXX and XXXX we think everything is moving smoothly. XX/XX/XXXX we get final pre-closing disclosures that include escrow, we reach out and ask for the Escrow to be waived, we are told that they can do it but now there would be a .25 % fee totalling {$2000.00}. We explained that this was not disclosed to us at any point previous, and when we went to shop around for another mortgage company Huntington told us they would not refund our Rate Lock Deposit, thus compelling us to move forward with them as our lenders under threat of loosing the {$5900.00}. XX/XX/XXXX, Huntington representative XXXX tells us that they will now not be able to waive escrow at all, which adds a cost of {$1200.00} per month. This is troubling for us since we explained the way our income works. Our broker made representations up until XX/XX/XXXX that we qualify for an escrow waiver when, in fact, we do not ( based on underwriting criteria or lender guidelines ), weconsiderthis a misrepresentation of loan terms. TILA requires that disclosures be accurate, and significant changes in these terms, such as being ineligible for an escrow waiver, should have been clearly communicated to us before making decisions like locking in an interest rate. Material Changes in Loan Terms : Under Regulation Z, which implements TILA, lenders must disclose material changes in loan terms, especially before closing. If a promised featuresuch as an escrow waiverends up being denied, that could be a significant change, potentially affecting our monthly payments and total loan cost. The Ohio Homebuyer Protection Act adds further protectionOurmortgage broker misrepresented our eligibility for an escrow waiver or failed to disclose critical loan termssuch as fees, interest rates, or terms related to your rate lockthis could be a violation under the OHPA. Brokers are required to act in your best interest and provide full and accurate disclosures. Under OHPA, any deceptive, unfair, or misleading practices may lead to penalties for the broker and recourse for us as the borrower. In our case, our broker promised us an escrow waiver that underwriting later denied, this constitutes a misrepresentation if it was not properly qualified or contingent on underwriting approval.

text: I am writing to formally lodge a complaint against CrossCountry Mortgage and XXXX XXXX XXXX regarding predatory lending practices. I believe that CrossCountry has engaged in practices that violate my rights as a borrower, specifically under the Truth in Lending Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. ), the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( 12 U.S.C. 2601 et seq. ), and the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1602 ). I was not adequately informed about the true costs of my mortgage, including hidden fees that were not disclosed at the time of signing. I have been charged fees that appear to be excessive and not in line with industry standards, which I believe are a form of predatory lending. My attempts to seek clarification and resolve these issues with CrossCountry have been met with inadequate responses and a lack of transparency. I received a phone call from XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX stating that the original loan officer, XXXX XXXX asked him to give us a call. XXXX stated that XXXX wanted to check in with us to see how everything was going. The only reason we received this call was because CrossCountry had received our Revocation of Power of Attorney via certified mail. Prior to this, we have had no communication with anyone from CrossCountry after XX/XX/XXXX. During the call, XXXX asked if we, ( my husband, XXXX XXXX and I ) had any concerns. We shared that according to XXXX XXXX XXXX ; we were in default of our mortgage and needed assistance with making payments. XXXX asked us to send him an email with the loan number and he would investigate further. XXXX was emailed the requested information the same day, and to date we have not heard back from him. The next correspondence that we received from CrossCountry was a 1099-C debt cancellation. This was a huge shock as we wondered what could have prompted CrossCountry to cancel the debt without any further communication. On Friday, XXXX, I was reviewing the Register of Deeds website for our county. I searched for our property address, and I learned that CrossCountry had assigned our Deed of Trust to XXXX XXXX XXXX and our title was given to XXXX XXXX XXXX. This was very concerning! The TILA act requires that borrowers be notified when their Deed of Trust debt has been sold, transferred, or assigned to a new creditor. Also, borrowers must be notified of the assignment and notification consists of contact information of the new creditor, recording dates, recording instrument numbers, changes in loan, etc. Needless to say, we received none of this. As far as we new, XXXX XXXX XXXX was the debt collector assigned to service our loan. As mentioned above, we mailed CrossCountry a notice of revocation of POA via certified mail on XX/XX/XXXX. A form 2848 was submitted to the IRS as well revoking all years, all periods. In addition to the 2848 being submitted to the IRS, we notified CrossCountry via certified mail that their POA was revoked, and they no longer had our permission to act on our behalf to include the right to transfer, the right to foreclose, the right to sell, the right to assign, etc. It is my belief that fraud has been committed and documents were forged granting them the authority to continue acting on our behalf. CrossCountry provided us with a 1099-C canceling the debt, and then assigned the Deed of Trust and title to XXXX XXXX XXXX. I believe that this was done in an attempt to cover the fraud and predatory lending that they have engaged in from the inception of this loan to date. I also believe that CrossCountrys goal was to redirect the attention from them to XXXX XXXX XXXX to escape any investigation of their practices. Both entities have engaged in unlawful practices and should be investigated.The XXXX number that I have obtained via audit reports will prove my claim.Despite the requests for debt validation, and validity of the promissory note, XXXX XXXX XXXX retained XXXX XXXX XXXX to begin foreclosure proceedings. XXXX was made aware that CrossCountry canceled the debt, and proof was provided. XXXX XXXX XXXX continues to threaten our family with foreclosure even though we were never properly notified via publication. XXXX did not run an ad in the local newspaper for three consecutive weeks as required by law, and this has been proven. Today, XX/XX/XXXX, I spoke with XXXX at the XXXX XXXX. XXXX searched our property address and informed me that after checking two separate areas, she did not see where publication for foreclosure had been filed. I also spoke with XXXX at the XXXX XXXX, and he too provided the same information. Despite all of this, XXXX XXXX XXXX, law firm for XXXX XXXX XXXX proceeded with assigning themselves as Trustee of our property in an attempt to move forward with foreclose. The next concern is that XXXX XXXX XXXX continues to identify themselves as Debt Collectors attempting to collect a debt. According to law, a Debt Collector can not foreclose on property. My original complaint states that the debt was never validated as evidenced by the draft which is being referred to as a promissory note. The promissory note is improperly classified due to its negotiable instrument characteristics. The note contains language such as " pay to the order of, '' indicating it is a draft, not a promissory note. An instrument containing an order to pay is not a promissory note. Proof : UCC 3-104 ( e ) ; " In re XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX. XXXX. XXXX XXXX ) ''. There is a Lack of Proof of Debt : CrossCountry nor Planet Home Lending have provided adequate proof that the note is a valid promissory note as previously requested. The burden of proof lies with XXXX XXXX XXXX and CrossCountry. The note 's characteristics make it ineligible to be used as evidence of debt. Proof : UCC 9-102 ( 65 ) ; Federal Reserve Act, Section 16 ( 38 Stat. 265 ) The terms of the promissory note are unconscionable and unenforceable. Proof : Principles of contract law and fairness promissory note. UCC 9-102 ( 65 ) : Defines a promissory note and excludes instruments with orders to pay. UCC 3-104 ( e ) : Clarifies that an instrument containing an order to pay is a draft. Establishes that a draft can not be utilized as evidence of an outstanding debt. These concerns will be forwarded to the IRS via form 3949-A, the FTC, and the SEC. In addition, this has had an adverse effect on my credit report due to the negative credit reporting which has deemed me as a potential risk to other creditors. These practices have affected my life, liberty, and pursuit of happiness. They have also caused significant financial distress and have undermined my ability to manage my mortgage responsibly. I believe these actions are predatory and violate federal and state lending laws designed to protect consumers.

I am writing to formally lodge a complaint regarding the wrongful foreclosure of my home. Net Present Value Calculation : There was no calculation of Net Present Value ( NPV ) conducted to determine our qualification for a loan modification. This is a crucial step in evaluating our case, and its absence indicates a lack of due diligence on the lenders part. 3. Bankruptcy Motion Notification : Prior to the auction sale, the trustee was notified of our motion to reopen Bankruptcy case # XXXX with the Central District Court XXXX This should have halted any foreclosure proceedings. 4. Overcharging for Services : Our account has been overcharged for services and fees that fall outside the terms of our loan agreement, exacerbating our financial distress. 6. Dual Tracking Practices : Despite submitting a Request for Mortgage Assistance, foreclosure activities were not halted. This dual tracking practice is not only unethical but also illegal. 7. Unreasonable Fees : We have incurred unreasonable fees charged to our mortgage account, which we believe are unjustifiable. 8. 2009 Payment Application Issues : In 2009, our payments were not properly applied, and despite our requests for a review, no action was taken to rectify the situation. 9. Foreclosure Rights : The current foreclosing party has no legitimate right to foreclose on our property, as the notice of sale was filed prior to the transfer or assignment of mortgage. Given these serious concerns, I kindly request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate this matter thoroughly. We are seeking restitution for the damages incurred due to these violations and hope to resolve this issue promptly. Thank you for your attention to this urgent matter. I look forward to your response.

Submitting a loss mitigation application without consent violates the duty to service the loan in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. Under the Truth in Lending Act ( XXXX ) and its implementing Regulation X, which governs mortgage servicing, mortgage servicers have specific obligations when handling loss mitigation applications. text: Dear CFPB, I am writing to formally lodge a complaint against Mr. Cooper, my mortgage servicer, for their repeated failure to comply with the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ), specifically 1024.17 ( c ) ( 1 ) ( ii ). I have been attempting to resolve these issues since XX/XX/XXXX, but despite my efforts, I continue to face significant problems with my escrow account and property tax payments and to date Mr.Cooper has not paid my town taxes once since XX/XX/XXXX. I closed on my home in XX/XX/XXXX with an FHA loan, at which time my previous mortgage company had partially paid a prorated portion of the town taxes. However, since Mr. Cooper took over my mortgage, they have failed to pay the town taxes repeatedly as required, despite clear stipulations in my closing documents indicating that this should have been handled through escrow. On XX/XX/XXXX I sent Mr Cooper a Tax Delinquent Notice via their XXXX email. I notified Mr Cooper that this was the second Delinquent notice I received. This notice shows that no town taxes had been paid for the XXXX fiscal year and the first bi annual tax payment was not paid. I received no response. The amount was {$2000.00} in owed taxes. In XX/XX/XXXX I spoke to XXXX customer service agents from Mr. Cooper online through their chat to figure out why my taxes were not paid. The first person I spoke to said my taxes were current and when I said they werent and that I had unpaid taxes I was told that the town tax was not escrowed with them. During closing for the home it was pointed out to me multiple times the house is double taxed with a town tax and a county tax and that both were escrowed with the mortgage and since such time I had been paying into the escrow monthly I knew what portion was for the town tax and what portion was for the County Tax. After pointing this out the customer service agent looked at my loan information, realized the error, and told me they created a ticket to get the town tax added to my escrow account and allegedly disburse the tax payment. They apparently only confirmed that my taxes were current. In XX/XX/XXXX I got the bi annual tax bill with the amount of past due taxes in {$2100.00} and current taxes due at XXXX. I sent this notice to Mr Cooper via their requested email. On XX/XX/XXXX I called Mr Cooper to ask why the town tax was not paid. After re-explaining the situation I was told to resend the bill which I did with the below description. I was told this issue would be escalated with the Tax team while they researched. I was told to resend this bill. I have spoken to customer service twice to resolve this, my loan closing documents show that my house is double taxed with a county tax and a town tax and clearly shows what amount I pay for both into escrow each month. Mr Cooper bought my mortgage and has only disbursed my county tax and my town tax is over a year delinquent. This is very concerning. The first customer service person I spoke to regarding this said it would get added and disbursed a month ago. It appears all they did was confirm county tax was current, which I didnt ask. Attached is the delinquent town tax that I pay to Mr Cooper into my escrow, every month. I am requesting the town tax be added to my escrow, as it should have been the duration of my mortgage after Mr Cooper bought it, and pay the town tax including fees and interest which you would have to contact the town treasurer to figure out what portion is fines and interest. I attached the last breakdown of fees and interest that I sent previously, but these are out of date as another due date has passed and more has accrued. Thank you. In XX/XX/XXXX, I was led to believe the issue had been resolved and a check was mailed to the town from Mr. Cooper for roughly in the amount of {$4000.00} intended to cover current taxes, back taxes, fines, and penalties. During this time I was mailed an escrow surplus check and told I have an escrow shortage. I deposited the escrow surplus check back into escrow to not have an increase in my monthly payment. In XX/XX/XXXX I was mailed another escrow surplus check. I called Mr Cooper to verify this was a true surplus check or if I should deposit back in escrow. After some research I was notified by voicemail that it was a true surplus check and I applied it as a principal payment to my mortgage. On XX/XX/XXXX I received the bi annual tax bill showing a past due amount of {$3200.00} and current due taxes of XXXX for a total of {$4200.00}. I called Mr Cooper to ask why I am getting a bill for taxes that were paid in XXXX. A ticket was started to research this. During the call I was notified that my monthly payment would be going up {$140.00} per month due to an escrow shortage. When I asked why, if my taxes were all figured out in XXXX, why am I having a shortage now after being assured the check I received in XXXX was truly a surplus check. The customer service agent looked at the details and told me that when the check was mailed in XXXX and taken from my escrow account, that payment amount of {$2700.00} ( Which was purely back taxes ) was the same amount that was disbursed on XX/XX/XXXX which is triple the taxes that were due. This error almost emptied my escrow and created a shortage and caused the increase in monthly payment. On XX/XX/XXXX I called the commissioner of revenue for my town and asked if they had ever received payment because I was assured a check was sent and that I was current. The commissioner told me that no payment has been received since XX/XX/XXXX when a partial amount was paid at closing. I called Mr Cooper to notify them and asked how that can be and the customer service agent told me that this check was returned, and the funds were never reinstated to my escrow account for 3 months while I was being told I have a shortage. My escrow account has XXXX entities to pay, not including XXXX. XXXX tax of {$970.00} XXXX XXXX XXXX of {$900.00} XXXX XXXX XXXX of {$900.00} Hazard insurance of {$520.00} My town can auction my home when delinquent XXXX year on taxes, this milestone has passed in XX/XX/XXXX. These ongoing issues have caused me significant distress and financial strain, and I believe they represent a violation of my rights under RESPA. Despite my repeated inquiries and attempts to resolve these matters directly with Mr. Cooper, I have not received adequate responses or solutions nor returned monies for improper disbursements and payments from my escrow account. I have to really wonder if these actions are not just a violation of my rights as a timely paying homeowner, but outright illegal or theft. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate these practices and take appropriate action to ensure compliance with RESPA. I am hopeful for a resolution that will rectify my escrow account and restore my faith in the mortgage servicing process. I request that Mr Cooper pay my year and a half delinquent town taxes that I have been paying to them monthly, interest and penalty accrued at Mr Coopers negligence, current taxes due, and close my escrow account. Thank you for your attention to this matter. Please feel free to contact me at the phone number or email address listed above if you require any further information.

And when I asked if I could go to a branch to communicate this matter in person, the representative expressed to me that the employees in the branch will not be able to help me in this particular case and that the best they could do is call the customer service number.

This is to notify you of all the issues we have faced since Shellpoint started servicing our HELOC, and to address our extremely urgent request to remove the delinquency status on our account so that we can withdraw funds. XX/XX/XXXX : Two more disbursement checks ( totaling ~ $ XXXX ) were returned due to the same reason above. We made a 3rd call to Shellpoint with no help from the agent and had to escalate to a manger for help. The manager told us that the hold on our HELOC account is permanent and that we need to send a dispute request through the Shellpoint portal ( online ) for them to investigate and correct the issue. He also mentioned that it will take at least 5 days to receive the request and for them to start investigating. We submitted our request immediately after the call. XX/XX/XXXX : We called to check the status of the request and were told that they received our request, but it could now take up to 30 days. The agent also told us that we will not be notified if/when the issue is resolved and that we must call daily, if we wanted to, to know the status. XX/XX/XXXX : On our call today to inquire about the status of our request and account, the agent told us that they have not received any request from us regarding our account. Our HELOC account should never have been in a delinquent status in the first place. If the account was put in a delinquent status due to a Shellpoint system issue, it should have been automatically removed when the payments were correctly posted to the account. We shouldnt have had to make a separate request to remove the delinquency status as its directly associated with the payment posting error from Shellpoint. Due to this error from Shellpoint, we are now in a difficult position where our payment to the vendor has been delayed and they might be sending our account to collections. text: I timely submitted to SPS a Complete Loss Mitigation application to SPS ; SPS acknowledged the Complete Loss Mitigation Application on XX/XX/XXXX. Despite the fact that loss mitigation is pending, SPS has scheduled a sale of my home for XX/XX/XXXX. There mere fact that a sale has been scheduled while loss mitigation is ongoing is DUAL TRACKING which is prohibited. It clearly states in SPSs own communication to me that because a Complete Loss Mitigation Application has been submitted and is being reviewed Im entitled to foreclosure protections and SPS will instruct the foreclosing attorney to postpone the scheduled sale. Since SPS has filed a Non-Judicial Foreclosure sale for XX/XX/XXXX, and there are no courts involved, there is absolutely no reason they are not able to postpone the sale and abide by their own words sent in the letter dated XX/XX/XXXX and highlighted below. This is a blatant and obvious RESPA violation. SPS received your complete Assistance Review Application, including all required information and documentation necessary to evaluate your account for loss mitigation assistance on XX/XX/XXXX. We expect to complete our evaluation within XXXX ( XXXX ) days of the date we received the complete Assistance Review Application. All options are offered at no cost to our customers and may include structured repayment plans, loan modifications, payment deferrals, or loan settlement alternatives. If your property also secures other accounts, you should consider contacting the servicer ( s ) of those accounts to discuss available loss mitigation options. You are entitled to certain foreclosure protections because we have received a complete Assistance Review Application. We will not proceed with filing of the first legal action, filing a motion for judgment, filing an order of sale or conduct a sale prior to evaluating your complete Assistance Review Application. If a foreclosure sale has already been scheduled, we will instruct our attorney to file a motion to postpone such sale. It is possible, however, that a court will deny the motion and the sale will proceed. If that happens, we will be unable to provide loss mitigation. I am also in receipt of SPSs mortgage statement dated XX/XX/XXXX, claiming {$11000.00} in charges/fees for Other Charges and Fees. I am assuming that there are other XXXX fees and costs assessed to my account in prior months. As Im sure SPS is aware, RESPA prohibits charging borrowers 3rd party fees if the work if not actually performed. Specifically, 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( b ) ( 5 ) requires that the servicer may only charge bona fide fees ; fees that the servicer determined it had a reasonable basis to impose. The mortgage company then deemed the property abandoned ( which it was not ) and changed the locks, not once but twice before filing for foreclosure. The first instance took place before the 120 days required for a mortgage to be past due and without judicial filing ( XXXX XXXX ). The second instance took place on or about XX/XX/XXXX, with clear signage and contact information posted on the front door where the locks were to be changed again, stating that the Property Was NOT Abandoned, in addition to numerous emails from my attorney to further advise the status of the property. During these illegal possessions of the property by The Bank, the property was repeatedly looted and vandalized by agents of the property management company. This resulted in the loss of valuable and irreplaceable family heirlooms and further destruction of personal property as well as further destruction of the physical property. When foreclosure was filed XX/XX/XXXX, The Bank held the entirety of the Insurance Disbursement resulting from the fire damage to the property in the amount of {$160000.00} which The Bank had held since XX/XX/XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, an offer of short payoff based on an independent appraisal was submitted to XXXX for The Bank, over a month prior to the foreclosure filing by said XXXX. The foreclosure process was allowed to take place up to XX/XX/XXXX when The Bank took funds from the XXXX XXXX ( {$100000.00} ), without my or my attorney 's knowledge, to pay off the mortgage, dismiss the foreclosure and release the lien. This could be construed as " Dual Tracking '' because a specific answer to the short sale offer was never given up until this point and ongoing as of this complaint. At the time of the dismissal of the foreclosure action in part, there was at that point {$28000.00} remaining from the Insurance Disbursement that The Bank still has yet to remit to me in excess of a YEAR later. RESPA 1024.34 explicitly prohibits this and states that they have 20 days to remit any funds under their control not including weekends and holidays. They were aware in emails with my attorney that they should remit said funds but have failed to do so. This act alone has prevented me from performing any necessary major further loss mitigation efforts or repairs to the property as well as prevented me from recovering {$78000.00} in recoverable depreciation from the insurance company. The Bank has at various times and in several ways completely and flagrantly denied my rights as successor in interest to the property. It can be construed through the ongoing state litigation of this matter that they are still to this day in denial of my rights under RESPA 1024.30. The Bank, having over double the principal balance of the loan as it was at the time of my Mothers Passing ( {$81000.00} ), Forced me to pay for additional Hazard insurance on the already damaged by fire property for an insured amount ( {$240000.00} ) just shy of 3 times that of the outstanding principal. This act is so unfathomable that there are not any specific laws regarding something like it. How is it legal for a lender to force place hazard insurance on a property in an amount nearly three times the outstanding principal, that is already damaged and their interests covered by that of a previous insurance policy while holding double the amount needed to protect their full interest if need be. Adding up all of these actions that are in direct violation of RESPA should result in major civil penalties. The question is will they? By my calculations and application of 12 U.S.C. 5565. Tier 3 penalties for Knowingly committing these violations should be at a ridiculous level as of the time of this complaint being filed. As of XXXX XXXX XXXX calculated at the adjusted inflation of the Tier XXXX penalty rate of up to {>= $1,000,000} per day, the RESPA 1024.34 violation of failure to remit the {$28000.00} to me alone, totals 268 days ( 401 calendar days ) at maximum penalty rate, over {$370.00} XXXX dollars and is ongoing daily. The failure to confirm and acknowledge my status as Successor In Interest to the property is 602 days ( XXXX calendar days ) from XX/XX/XXXX as of XX/XX/XXXX. There is absolutely no excuse that would have any shred of conceivable merit for actions like this to be allowed to happen when every lender has internal compliance offices that are tasked with making sure that the laws enacted under RESPA are followed exactingly. Complaint Against PHH Mortgage for Violating Rights Under Negotiable Instrument Law and Other Federal Regulations PHH Mortgage Loan Number : XXXX Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am filing this complaint regarding PHH Mortgage 's handling of my loan, specifically related to their disregard for applicable negotiable instrument laws, as outlined in the Texas Business & Commerce Code ( Section 3.104 ) and other federal statutes. These instruments are legally binding under Texas law, yet PHH Mortgage has failed to meet its fiduciary responsibilities about these transactions. PHH Mortgages actionsthrough freezing my account and threatening mealso interfere with my rights under 15 U.S.C. Chapter 41, which ensures that I have the right to informed use of credit. Their aggressive tactics, which suggest I am engaging in fraudulent activities, are not only unfounded but constitute potential libel and slander. If this behavior continues, I intend to pursue legal action and hold them accountable for these violations. Furthermore, PHH is legally obligated to present the negotiable instruments I have endorsed and tendered for payment under Texas Business and Commerce Code, Section 3.501. PHH Mortgages refusal to process these instruments and their failure to meet their legal obligations under federal and state law is why I am bringing this issue to the CFPB 's attention. On XX/XX/year>, Fay Servicing responded to my complaint # XXXX. However, they have yet to address my primary concern regarding when and why my FHA loan was purportedly converted to a conventional loan. At no point did I sign or agree to any change in the loans terms, nor was I notified of such a conversion. Without my explicit agreement, the loan you currently manage is not my original loan, as I did not authorize or initiate any conversion from FHA to conventional terms. Rebranding this loan with a new loan number and claiming it as conventional, without my consent, constitutes identity theft. The discontinuation of FHA insurance does not equate to a conversion of the loan from FHA to conventional terms. The FHAs 601 Accelerated Claims Disposition ( ACD ) program, also known as the Joint Venture or Note Sales Program, does not automatically convert an FHA loan into a conventional loan. Instead, the ACD allows FHA to sell delinquent loans to private investors to resolve these loans outside FHAs insurance framework. Once the loan is sold, it no longer carries FHA insurance, and the investor can then explore various outcomes, such as loan modifications or even foreclosures, based on the terms of sale and neighborhood stabilization requirements. However, this sale to an investor under ACD does not constitute a refinancing process or imply that the loan has been converted from FHA to conventional. For a loan to become conventional, a formal refinance process must occur, where new loan terms are explicitly agreed upon between the borrower and the lender, and FHA insurance is formally removed. The ACD program is designed to provide flexibility in managing defaulted loans but does not inherently alter the loan type from FHA to conventional. The Distressed Asset Stabilization Program ( DASP ) similarly provides FHA the ability to sell severely delinquent loans to investors who aim to stabilize the property and neighborhood. This program allows investors the flexibility to offer borrower assistance programs, such as principal reduction or interest rate limits, to help avoid foreclosure. However, DASP does not convert an FHA loan into a conventional loan ; it simply transfers ownership, allowing the new loan holder to assess modification options as part of stabilization efforts. For further details, the HUD website and related program fact sheets provide an in-depth explanation of both the ACD and DASP programs and the responsibilities of investors under these programs. Your response lacks a specific timeline, justification, or documentation evidencing my consent to this alleged conversion, which remains central to my inquiry. I request this documentation and reiterate that no consent has been given to rebrand or change the loan to conventional terms.
