In XX/XX/year>, my client attempted to sell her home in XXXX, NY. However, during this process, we identified multiple instances of fraudulent misrepresentation on the mortgage application submitted by Meadowbrook Financial. Additionally, we discovered an inaccurate appraisal that inflated the propertys value by over {$75000.00}. The seller and the buyer were once friends, leading the buyer to share his entire mortgage application with the sellera document he seems to have forgotten about. Currently, the buyer is claiming he was always a part-owner of the property, despite his signed FHA Identity of Interest form , where he explicitly stated there was no family or business relationship with the seller. A copy of this signed document is attached. This document also differs from his notarized sworn court document which state that the property was purchased as an investment ( see statement attached ). If this is the case, which is not, should have indicated that this was a business transaction, which would have not allowed him to take advantage of the 3.5 % down payment. This was all overseen by the mortgage broker. Furthermore, the buyer falsely claimed on his mortgage application that he had lived in the property for eight years, despite the fact that my client did not own the home for that length of time. It's likely that the buyer lied about his residency to appear more stable to lenders, who often see longer occupancy as a sign of financial responsibility and lower lending risk. In reality, the property was tenant-occupied, which was one of the reasons the seller was unable to deliver the home. Meadowbrook oversaw the entire application process. The application is also attached. The appraisal was completed by XXXX XXXX in XXXX, NY ( Meadowbrook Financial was also present ) and failed to meet the guidelines of HUD. Specifically, the report incorrectly lists the house as having two and a half bathrooms, which is entirely false. In reality, the .5 bathroom is only a small niche in the mudroom with two walls and a toilet. There are no other bathroom fixtures in that area, and without a sink, it can not be classified as a half bathroom. Additionally, the appraisal diagram inaccurately shows a garage with a " bedroom '' a few feet away. In reality, no such bedroom exists ; the space in question is a mudroom. Not only does this area fail to meet XXXX XXXX definition of a bedroom, but it also serves as the only access to the non-habitable garage which is actually depicted on the buyer 's appraisal report. According to XXXXXXXX XXXX guidelines, a bedroom can not act as a passageway to another space, such as a garage. As a result, the home was listed as a three-bedroom with an accessory unit, when in reality, it should have been classified as a two-bedroom home, if the additional section even qualified as an accessory apartment, which it does not. The so-called accessory apartment, located on the right side of the house, also fails to meet XXXXXXXX XXXX requirements for accessory apartments. The appraiser would have known this had he properly inspected the space, but he neither entered the area nor took any photos of it- Meadowbrook was also present during this inspection. The " kitchen '' shown in the diagram does not conform to XXXXXXXX XXXX definition of a kitchen for an accessory apartment. The appraisal report attributed {$30000.00} of value to a so-called " accessory apartment '' unit, which only added to the pattern of fraudulent assessments. This is wholly against HUDs stringent rules on appraisals which indicate inspectors must access ALL rooms in a dwelling. Amidst these inaccuracies, one truthful statement stood out : the appraisal report correctly classified the transaction as non-arms-length, acknowledging the personal ( but not familial ) relationship between the buyer and seller. This detail is crucial, as FHA guidelines explicitly prohibit a gift of equity in such situations. Gifts of equity can only come from family members, and yet, no one raised this issue. Despite this key restriction, Meadowbrook Financial, insisted on including the gift of equity in the contract. Their blatant disregard for FHA guidelines highlights the fraudulent nature of the entire transaction. Upon further inspection, the appraisal report raised more concerns. The appraiser included several misleading photos. One image, labeled as a bedroom, is actually a small sitting area open to the first floor like a balcony. The mudroom was mislabeled as an office in the report, yet on the diagram, it was depicted as the bedroom. These falsifications greatly inflated the home 's value, further undermining the integrity of the appraisal process. Since my client did not consent to signing the contract, the issue has escalated to litigation, costing her over {$40000.00} in legal fees and nearly {$100000.00} in urgent home safety renovationsissues that were deliberately omitted from the reports. For example, many outlets had live grounding wires ; without proper grounding, a lightning strike could have electrified the entire house, posing a deadly fire risk. This mortgage fraud includes- Residence fraud Appraisal fraud Gift of Equity fraud This matter has now been reported to the FBI and the Office of the Inspector General and will soon be brought to the attention of the New York State Attorney General.

text: Back in the beginning of XX/XX/XXXX, I submitted my documentation and payment to have my PMI removed with my mortgage servicer, NewRez. I was instructed to pay the fee ( {$190.00} ) for the valuation of my home to determine if PMI could be removed. Makes no sense. I had to go through the process again and request they expedite me another form to sign and email in. I received the form, signed and emailed it in. Within a few days I received correspondence that my document was received, and I would hear from an external appraiser about scheduling the valuation within 14 calendar days. Another 21 calendar days went by, I heard nothing, so I reached back out to NewRez yet again. I reached out via the company 's chat function, and when I requested a number for someone I could contact regarding this issue, I was told " There is no one that you can talk to. '' A few days after that, I received a letter in the mail that stated PMI was removed AFTER AN ACCOUNT REVIEW WAS PERFORMED. Never was I told a simple account review had to be done! This company deceived me into paying {$190.00} for a valuation of my home, just for a simple account review to be performed. I contacted them yet again, because nowhere in the early removal paperwork did it say an account review could be performed. When I asked about having that fee returned, I was told I would have to file a dispute. I did that on/around XXXX. As of today, XX/XX/XXXX, I have received no correspondence that my dispute was received and is being reviewed. I have received no communication as to the status of my dispute, and I can not get a hold of anyone in customer service to determine the status of my dispute. I currently see a $ XXXX sitting in my account dashboard, but I can't get anyone to tell me what that is for ( I can only assume it is a refund for my fee payment ). Additionally, my XXXX statement is not available, so I can not determine if this is going to be applied to my monthly payment or if I will receive it as a refund. I believe the whole PMI removal process was a violation of UDAAP as it is completely deceptive ; all I needed was an account review and I wouldn't have had to go through this whole process. The amount of time I have spent between being on the chat with the company, sending emails through their Contact Us function, and attempting to call and getting circled back in the phone menu to literally no one has cost me WELL OVER {$190.00} of my time, and now I have no access to my periodic statement? Is my statement being unavailable also not a violation of the Truth in Lending Act, 12 CFR 1026.41? At this time, the only resolution I request is my {$190.00} to be returned to me via check. If I could utilize a different servicer, I absolutely would but that is out of my hands at this point as well. I attempted to remove the PMI to save some money, and the time-suck and frustration I have gone through is not acceptable for any consumer. Thank you for your time.

Since my mortgage was transferred from US Bank to XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ), my efforts to secure financial hardship assistance have been met with significant obstacles. When US Bank held my loan, I was already in the process of applying for hardship relief due to financial difficulties. However, the transfer to XXXX interrupted this process, and I was informed that I would need to reapply for assistance. In light of this, I believe XXXX conduct violates several established legal standards set forth in relevant case law, as well as federal requirements under the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ) : 1. Failure to Provide Required Hardship Applications Under XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ), servicers are legally required to facilitate the loan modification review process with transparency, providing clear timelines and communicating effectively with borrowers. By failing to deliver the application materials needed to complete my hardship request, XXXX is impeding my right to apply for loss mitigation assistance. Additionally, XXXX XXXX. XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) established that servicers must review loss mitigation options prior to initiating foreclosure. The ongoing notices on my door and constant phone calls create an atmosphere of pressure, suggesting potential foreclosure, which violates my right to a fair review process for hardship assistance. 2. Failure to Communicate Effectively and Harassment Concerns In XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ), the court reinforced the requirement for servicers to communicate clearly under RESPA. This means that XXXX should be responding to my inquiries with specific information and documentation regarding my application. The repeated verbal assurances without follow-up action fall short of this standard. Additionally, the ongoing phone calls and physical notices could be deemed harassing, given that my application remains unresolved. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) reinforces that servicers are required to notify borrowers of any substantial actions that could affect their rights, such as placing insurance or initiating foreclosure, with clarity and fairness. XXXX failure to provide a hardship application while simultaneously issuing foreboding notices directly contravenes this requirement, subjecting me to undue stress and uncertainty. XXXX. Escrow Account Mismanagement and Failure to Pay Taxes/Insurance Under RESPA, servicers managing escrow accounts are required to ensure that all escrowed payments, including taxes and insurance, are made in a timely manner. XXXX also touched upon servicers obligations regarding insurance, and XXXX failure to meet its duty to pay my taxes and insurance represents a severe oversight. By not applying the funds from my escrow account appropriately, XXXX is exposing me to potential lapses in insurance and delinquency on property taxesboth of which could have long-term financial consequences and even jeopardize my property ownership. Next Steps and Potential Remedies I plan to file a Qualified Written Request ( QWR ) under RESPA to formally demand that XXXX address these issues in writing. In this QWR, I will request : Immediate delivery of the hardship application, with a clear timeline for review and a specific contact point for any additional documentation they might require. A detailed accounting of the escrow account to clarify why my taxes and insurance have not been paid, along with XXXX explanation for this failure to comply with the terms initially managed by US Bank. An explanation of why I am receiving foreclosure-related notices and phone calls while still awaiting the hardship application, which should pause any collection or foreclosure activity until my application is resolved. In parallel, I am considering filing a complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ). The CFPB has the authority to investigate and enforce consumer protection laws, including RESPA, especially where there are patterns of servicing abuse as evidenced in cases like XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX. This complaint will outline XXXX failure to follow established protocols, harassment through undue notices, and mishandling of my escrow account. Finally, if these issues persist, I will seek legal counsel to explore the possibility of a RESPA claim against XXXX. This claim could potentially provide for : Damages : Compensation for any financial losses resulting from XXXX failure to fulfill its servicer obligations, including penalties associated with missed tax and insurance payments. Injunctive Relief : A court order compelling XXXX to handle my application fairly, communicate clearly, and ensure proper use of my escrow account. Attorneys Fees : Since RESPA allows for recovery of legal fees if I prevail, XXXX may also be liable for the costs incurred to rectify their noncompliance. In conclusion, XXXX actions appear to contravene multiple consumer protection standards and legal precedents established to prevent precisely this type of servicing abuse. I am experiencing issues with my mortgage servicer, RoundPoint Mortgage Servicing LLC, regarding the removal of escrow and Private Mortgage Insurance ( PMI ) from my mortgage account. Despite fulfilling all specified requirements, including maintaining a Loan-to-Value ( LTV ) ratio well below the required 80 %, RoundPoint Mortgage has repeatedly added new conditions, delayed the process, and provided conflicting information, preventing the removal of both PMI and escrow. Complaint Details : Initial Request and Requirements Fulfilled : On XX/XX/year>, I requested to have the escrow removed from my mortgage. RoundPoint acknowledged receipt of my request on XX/XX/XXXX at XXXXXXXX XXXX. and informed me that PMI would need to be removed first to proceed. I submitted a request to remove PMI and provided all necessary documentation, including a Broker Price Opinion ( BPO ) that confirmed my LTV is well below the 80 % threshold required for PMI removal. The BPO was completed and returned to RoundPoint on XX/XX/year>, as confirmed by the broker who submitted it. Repeated Delays and Added Stipulations : Despite meeting the required conditions, RoundPoint has repeatedly delayed the process by introducing new, uncommunicated stipulations. Most recently, on XX/XX/year>, RoundPoint added a requirement that PMI and escrow can not be removed because the property is located in a FEMA-designated disaster area. This FEMA-related stipulation was never disclosed in prior communications or outlined in my mortgage documents. Each time I fulfill a requirement, RoundPoint imposes additional stipulations, effectively preventing the timely removal of PMI and escrow. This pattern of continually moving the goalposts appears to be a tactic to maintain escrow and PMI, creating undue frustration and financial burden. Escrow Payment Increase Without Adjustment : My monthly mortgage payment increased from {$3600.00} to {$4300.00} due to a significant rise in my propertys assessed value. If the property value had not increased, this payment adjustment would not have occurred. Despite this, my Homestead Credit has not been applied, and my escrow payments have only increased with no reduction or adjustment, contrary to CFPB Regulation 1024.17, which governs escrow maintenance and adjustments. Similar Complaints from Other Customers : Through research, I found multiple similar complaints from other RoundPoint Mortgage customers, who have faced similar delays and additional requirements when attempting to remove PMI and escrow. These practices appear to be systemic and designed to prevent timely removal of these obligations. Request for Resolution : I am seeking the CFPBs assistance to : Ensure RoundPoint Mortgage complies with federal regulations and my mortgage agreement, particularly regarding escrow adjustments and the removal of PMI. Obtain immediate removal of PMI and escrow based on my LTV compliance and the fulfillment of all disclosed requirements. Investigate RoundPoint Mortgages practices concerning delays, additional stipulations, and FEMA-related restrictions that were not previously disclosed, to ensure fair treatment of all customers. Supporting Documentation : Copies of all communication with RoundPoint Mortgage regarding PMI and escrow removal. BPO verifying my LTV is below 80 %. Documentation of payment increase due to property value reassessment.

text: On or about XX/XX/year>, I applied for a HELOC with Bank of America. Each requested document was supplied within the same day or the next day after the request. On XX/XX/XXXX, one month later, I received notification that my application was " deactivated. After my application was deactivated, I then received requests for about a dozen new documents not previously requested in order to reactivate my application, which I supplied within the same day on XX/XX/XXXX. Today is XXXX XXXX, and my application is still pending. I confirmed this morning that there is no further information required of me. I dont understand what is happening here -- I have significant annual income and assets, and the property being offered as collateral has ample equity at least 80 % of the FMV . I have been a XXXX XXXX XXXX for over 22 years, and I own a very successful XXXX XXXX XXXX. I have applied for mortgages and lines of credits many times before, and I've helped many clients in the process as well. I have never been asked to provide so much information, nor have I ever waited so long for a decision. When I ask for the status of my application, I always receive an answer, but it is always vague. When I ask follow up questions regarding the next ( remaining ) steps in the process, I don't receive a satisfactory answer. Today I was told that they are just waiting on one payoff amount, BUT I have already provided all of the payoff information requested in the form of the most current billing statements, the account numbers, PINS and the addresses of the financial institutions. I also happen to know that they have already called the bank that has my current HELOC, because I received a call from a representative of that bank weeks ago. In total, the process described above, which has not yet resulted in a credit decision, has so far taken eight weeks with no end in sight. I regret applying to BOA, and believe I could have had the approval and probably the funds by now if I had applied elsewhere. But with so much time invested, I am hanging in there with this application process. I have more comments about the level of financial competency of the people I've been dealing with, but I am more dissatisfied with the lack of transparency of the process. Even though they are always giving an " answer '', it is always vague and confusing. When I ask follow up questions to clarify the process, I am always told they don't know or can't answer that question. Pennymac claims to have business values of " accountability, reliability, and ethical behavior. '' However, their online customer payment system, email communications and predatory, spam-oriented sales practices are systematically designed to increase fees and sales- not protect consumers. Their practices resulted in a first mortgage late fee ever and a 'ding ' on our credit report - reducing our ability to refinance once rates drop sufficiently. They've profited from arranging anti-consumer systems and thus cost our family precious dollars. We, as consumers with previously perfect credit payment histories, changed bank accounts for autopay. The online system apparently *SKIPS* paying your current month, moving your next payment to AFTER the current one due. There is no reason their system can't accept a payment- yet it didn't and I missed a payment, resulting in a late fee and 30 day late on my credit. Apparently there is some website text we missed, putting the 'blame ' for this systemic failure on the consumer. Normally, I would have acted upon any communication from Pennymac about my late payment, allowing me to correct the problem in time. And, indeed, at some point during the month ( 18 days after I missed a payment ), there was one email in my spam folder about a payment being missed. However, they also buried us in sales spam after rates dropped in XXXX, resulting on the one email being filtered as spam. In an ethical company, service practices and communications are focused on serving the customers paying for services. However, during the month which the online system skipped my payment, mortgage rates dropped a little bit. Pennymac sent us sales emails ( and texts and calls ) every couple of days, relentlessly. Examples of just the emails I have copies include : XXXX : Call now to save XXXX : You can save up to {$210.00} per month ( to me ) XXXX : You can save up to {$210.00} per month ( to husband ) XXXX : URGENT, you can lower your payments ( to me ) XXXX : URGENT, you can lower your payments ( to husband ) XX/XX/XXXX : IMPORTANT : Call now to save ( to me ) XX/XX/XXXX : IMPORTANT : Call now to save ( to husband ) XX/XX/XXXX : You can save up to {$310.00} a month ( to me ) XX/XX/XXXX : You can save up to {$310.00} a month ( to husband ) XX/XX/XXXX : URGENT :, you can lower your monthly payment ( to me ) XX/XX/XXXX : URGENT :, you can lower your monthly payment ( to husband ) XX/XX/XXXX : Your monthly payment reminder - Hi At Pennymac, we make it quick and convenient for you to access your account. '' - no mention of late payment due XX/XX/XXXX : XX/XX/XXXX : Your monthly payment reminder - At Pennymac, we make it quick and convenient for you to access your account. " - no mention of late payment due XX/XX/XXXX : You can save up to {$120.00} per month ( to me ) XX/XX/XXXX : You can save up to {$120.00} per month ( to husband ) XX/XX/XXXX : URGENT :, you can lower your monthly payment ( to me ) XX/XX/XXXX : URGENT :, you can lower your monthly payment ( to husband ) XXXX : Payment Due Reminder - the only email stating we missed a payment, buried in predatory sales spam and flooding into my spam folder*** XX/XX/XXXX : IMPORTANT : Call now to save up to {$1400.00} per year ( me ) XX/XX/XXXX : IMPORTANT : Call now to save up to {$1400.00} per year ( husband ) XX/XX/XXXX : Monthly statement notice XX/XX/XXXX : Your mortgage payment- At Pennymac, we make it quick and convenient for you to access your account. '' ( to me ) - no mention of late payment due XX/XX/XXXX : Your mortgage payment - At Pennymac, we make it quick and convenient for you to access your account. '' ( to husband ) - no mention of late payment due XX/XX/XXXX : : A new home? We can help you make it happen XX/XX/XXXX : A new home? We can help you make it happen Many of the SALES EMAILS indicate a " time sensitive alert. '' The " mortgage payment '' emails do not reference missed payments nor time sensitive info. Clearly, communications are geared toward revenue and flooding customers with spam - effectively hiding the late payment information until after they can charge fees. Finally on XXXX, after reporting us to credit as more than 30 days late, they sent us a " DOCUMENT NOTICE OF LATE PAYMENT '' that came through, not as spam. They could, apparently, sent such a notice at any point, but instead sent us sales communications. And, during this same period, we got call after call and text after text of refi offers. Pennymac has, very obviously, designed their online user interface and payment system to skip same month auto pays changes, likely because they receive extra late fee revenue. They designed predatory, spam oriented email campaigns to BURY real customer communications, making it difficult to act upon actual account information. This company 's day to day practices are a threat to the very consumer protections put into place after XXXX. I tried twice to explain the payment missed was an ERROR due to the way their system is set up. I protested a lack of notification of their system SKIPPING our payment. The supervisor I spoke to at Pennymac scolded me, noting they have **no obligation to remind consumers a payment was late and they do not have to email anyone. ** He also lied, stating Pennymac has no control over reporting a payment as late or not, despite systems issues or failures to communicate with customers. Further, he said our inability to filter the single late payment notice from the flood of spam was our fault, since we didn't know to opt out. Yet, Pennymac profited off our late fee and will continue to profit off our inability to, in the future, refinance at a lower rate b/c our credit score was lowered. They benefit, we suffer, and yet their system failures, designed by Pennymac, are at fault. The company should be required to fix both it's predatory, fee-making auto-pay system and be required to send a series of clear, correct, highly discriminable consumer communications about late or missed payments. That is the only way to build trust with consumers ( NOT communications for profit ), and protect those same customers. Their response to our issue is shameful. And, I want any 'late payment ' negative report moved from my husband and I 's credit report. I'd like a refund of the late fee. Systemic practices such as these continue to threaten consumer financial well-being during one of the most costly financial eras of our lifetimes. I did not miss a payment. **I arranged an ontime payment** and Pennymac 's user interface and designed MOVED move my next payment to the following month- and they designed the system.

text: Complaint Against NewRez LLC Regarding Collection Activity and Inactive MERS Status This letter serves as a final notice and formal complaint against NewRez LLC regarding continued collection activity despite their inactive status in the MERS ( Mortgage Electronic Registration Systems ) under Servicer ID XXXX. I am the trustee of the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, with fiduciary responsibility to ensure all duties are met to protect the assets and rights of the Trust. Account Number : XXXX I am filing this complaint because MERS, the Mortgage Electronic Registration Systems, has been listed as inactive on my mortgage record for an extended periodover XXXX years, according to my records. Since MERS originally held the electronic title rights for my loan, this prolonged inactive status raises concerns about the clarity and accuracy of title ownership and recordkeeping. This creates uncertainty regarding who legally holds my mortgage, which could affect future servicing, title verification, and the Trust 's rights. I am requesting assistance to ensure my mortgage records are accurately maintained and to address any implications of MERS inactivity by my mortgage servicer. As trustee, I am formally requesting an immediate response and investigation due to the breach of trust and multiple violations of borrower rights under the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ) and the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) committed by NewRez LLC. Additionally, I am seeking setoff and restitution for all monthly payments made in good faith, specifically a refund of {$940.00} per month since XXXX, to address the financial hardship and unjust enrichment resulting from NewRezs inactive status. Please be advised that this request for restitution does not constitute a waiver of the Trust 's rights to pursue further compensation, restitution, and damages, as I am prepared to pursue court action if necessary. Summary of Violations and Timeline Inactive MERS Status : Shellpoints inactive status in MERS raises significant concerns regarding their authority to collect on this mortgage, as confirmed through recent MERS records. Continued Collection Despite Inactive Status : Despite being inactive, Shellpoint has continued monthly collections without disclosing this status, constituting a breach of trust and violating my fiduciary duties to protect the Trusts interests. Failure to Provide Documentation : Prior Qualified Written Requests ( QWR ) for essential documentation, including a MERS Milestone Report, have gone unanswered. This report is critical for verifying the mortgages ownership and servicing rights history and confirming NewRezs legal authority to act as servicer. Legal Violations, Breach of Trust, and Financial Restitution Failure to Verify Legal Right to Collect : Collection activities under an inactive MERS status, without validating NewRezs servicing rights, violate both RESPA and TILA, causing financial hardship to the Trust, as monthly payments have been made in good faith. Unjust Enrichment and Bad Faith : Continued collections under inactive status, without transparency, constitute unjust enrichment and reflect bad faith. Non-Response to QWR : NewRezs lack of response to the QWR and requested MERS Milestone Report further violates RESPAs requirements for timely responses, impacting my fiduciary ability to protect the Trusts assets. Requested Action I request that the CFPB take immediate action to : Obtain a MERS Milestone Report documenting all ownership and servicing changes for this mortgage. Confirm Shellpoints legal authority to collect payments while designated inactive in MERS. Provide the full set of origination and servicing documents, including the original agreement with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. Facilitate a setoff to balance the ledger for unjustly collected payments since XXXX and secure restitution of {$940.00} per month, in addition to my down payment of {$43000.00} as part of my " EQUITY '' in the property, along with additional compensation for financial hardship, unjust enrichment, and other damages resulting from Shellpoints actions. Remove any negative items inaccurately reported on my credit report to reflect an accurate account history. Total Equity and Investment with Reservation of Rights The total estimated investment and equity in this property is {$280000.00}, accounting for my down payment, monthly mortgage payments, costs for equipment, and maintenance expenses since XXXX. I am providing this calculation to establish my financial stake as the equitable owner and to reflect the full scope of my commitment and contributions. However, I explicitly reserve all rights to seek additional compensation for the emotional and financial hardships caused by NewRez LLCs actions. NewRez LLC has subjected me to considerable distress, financial hardship, and mental anguish. This includes sleepless nights, anxiety, and the ongoing stress of receiving default letters despite my rightful position as the XXXXquitable owner holding the highest title. Furthermore, their actions have jeopardized my sole source of income, threatening my ability to provide for my family and maintain stability. Additionally, NewRez LLC has violated my privacy by sending default letters directly to my tenant, which is a breach of trust, privacy, and a clear instance of bad faith. My commitment to fulfilling my obligations has been met with unjust enrichment on NewRezs part, as they continue to act without regard to the payments tendered and the value I have built in this property. I assert my rights to pursue further relief and compensation for all harms and injustices I have endured. This final notice seeks a prompt and comprehensive resolution. Please be advised that I am prepared to pursue court action if this matter remains unresolved. Furthermore, I am formally demanding the immediate removal of the incorrect negative items reported by NewRez LLC on my credit report. These inaccurate entries, including the erroneous XX/XX/XXXX negative item and other missing data points from XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, and the XXXX XXXX discrepancy, have caused my credit score to drop significantly and are imposing a financial burden. These inaccuracies not only harm my credit profile but also violate the standards of fair and accurate credit reporting as required under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681 ). I insist that NewRez LLC take swift action to investigate and permanently remove any inaccurate negative items from my credit report, ensuring that my account history is reported accurately and fairly. I expect a prompt resolution and written confirmation of the corrections. Enclosed you will find a recent copy of my credit report showing the negative items, as well as a copy of the MERS ServicerID which indicates NewRez LLCs inactive status.

Complaint Template for XXXX and CFPB Regarding Negligence by JPMorgan Chase on Home Loan Escrow Subject : Negligence in Escrow Handling Resulting in Double Payment and Financial Impact To Whom It May Concern : I am filing a formal complaint against JPMorgan Chase regarding their handling of my mortgage escrow account, which resulted in a double payment of homeowners insurance, an escrow shortfall, and increased monthly payments. Details of the Incident : Timeline of Communication : On XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted JPMorgan Chase through their customer service line regarding the removal of homeowners insurance payments from escrow on my mortgage account. On these calls ( recorded by Chase XXXX, I was assured multiple times that no future payments would be disbursed from escrow for homeowners insurance. Submission of Proof : On XX/XX/XXXX, I uploaded the required proof of payment and the policy document from our new homeowners insurance company to Chase, further confirming that the policy had been paid in full. Escrow Disbursement Error : Despite the reassurances from Chase, they disbursed a payment from the escrow account to the new insurance company after the policy had already been fully paid. This resulted in : A double payment for the policy. An escrow analysis shortfall, which increased my monthly mortgage payment as I am now effectively repaying the erroneously disbursed insurance payment each month. Legal and Regulatory Concerns : Violation of RESPA ( Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ) : Under 12 CFR 1024.17 ( k ), mortgage servicers are required to conduct escrow account management in a manner that ensures funds are disbursed accurately and timely, avoiding errors that could result in financial harm to the borrower. The double payment and resulting shortfall indicate negligence in escrow management. Misrepresentation and Negligence : Chase 's repeated assurances that no payments would be made, followed by their actions to the contrary, constitute misrepresentation. This may also violate consumer protection laws, such as 15 U.S.C. 45 under the Federal Trade Commission Act, which prohibits unfair or deceptive acts. Failure to Correct Errors : Under RESPA and related CFPB regulations, Chase has a duty to address and resolve errors in escrow accounts promptly once brought to their attention. Their failure to prevent or rectify this issue has caused financial and emotional distress. Impact on Me : The escrow shortfall caused by the double payment has unjustly increased my monthly mortgage payment. I have had to bear the burden of addressing this error despite assurances that the situation would not occur. This experience has significantly eroded my confidence in Chase 's ability to competently manage my mortgage account. Desired Resolution : Immediate Correction : Reimburse the escrow account for the disbursed funds to eliminate the shortfall and adjust my monthly payment back to its correct amount. Provide a detailed explanation and timeline of how the funds will be returned and the account corrected. Review and Improvement of Processes : Investigate the root cause of this error and ensure safeguards are in place to prevent similar incidents in the future. Compensation for Damages : Consider providing compensation for the financial inconvenience and stress caused by this situation. I trust that JPMorgan Chase will take this matter seriously and rectify the error promptly. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Hello, I have a loan through Wells Fargo Home Mortgage. My father passed away a year ago on the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, and ever since then I have been trying to assume our home mortgage loan because I am the sole beneficiary in our trust and I am responsible for all of my fathers assets, and financially responsible to take care of them. With this being said, Wells Fargo has taken me for a roller coaster ride of extreme difficulty and frustration since my fathers passing. They have repetitively told me that I can not assume our home mortgage loan without doing a numerous amount of steps, with which I began completing so that I could receive help from them. Although I never did receive any help from them and decided to make a couple of phone calls to lawyers asking about this process in more depth. I came to find out about the The Garn-St Germain Act . A transfer to a relative resulting from the death of a borrower. This situation involves the transfer of real property when one or more relatives inherits it after the borrowers death. If the beneficiaries are relatives, then the due-on-sale clause will not be enforced. No one ever explained this to me at Wells Fargo and I was told that I would have to assume the mortgage through numerous documents proving I was my fathers beneficiary and that I would not be able to get the same rate as him when I redid our mortgage and reapplied for it. I also was just told today that I am no longer allowed to make any sort of payment towards our mortgage unless I pay them {$27000.00} right away being the amount that would bring it current based on my fathers criteria. Subject : Formal Complaint Regarding Deceptive Business Practices, Misrepresentation, and Lack of Transparency in Home Purchase and Loan Process To Whom It May Concern, I am writing to file a formal complaint against Lennar XXXX ( the builder ) and Lennar Mortgage ( the lending entity ) concerning the home purchase and loan process for the property located at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, XXXX XXXX ( Loan Number : XXXX ). Both companies are part of the Lennar Corporation, but I believe they have engaged in deceptive business practices related to the {$21000.00} rate buy-down credit, lack of transparency in the loan terms, and miscommunication between their departments. XXXX. Misrepresentation of {$21000.00} Rate Buy-Down Credit From the outset, Lennar XXXX ( through their sales representatives and loan officers ) misrepresented the {$21000.00} rate buy-down credit. This credit was initially presented as a straightforward incentive to reduce the interest rate on the loan. However, after signing the agreement and seeking clarification from the loan officer, I was informed that it was being treated as a promotional rate or bulk rate buy-down. These terms were never disclosed upfront and were explained with insufficient details, using terms such as off settlement, bulk buy-down, and XXXX, which are not industry-standard and remain unclear to the consumer. These terms were neither defined in plain language nor adequately explained in the documents provided. At the time of the agreement, I explicitly confirmed with the loan officer that the {$21000.00} credit would be applied toward the rate buy-down. This was a key part of my decision to proceed with the purchase. Yet, at closing, I learned that the credit was not applied as promised and instead, Lennar referred to it as a promotional rate, further complicating and confusing the matter. This misrepresentation violates the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ), both of which require clear and accurate disclosures of loan terms, including how any credits are applied. XXXX. Lack of Transparency and Potential Deceptive Practices Throughout the process, Lennar failed to provide transparency regarding the nature of the {$21000.00} credit and the rate buy-down. The lack of clarity surrounding the credits application raises serious concerns about potential deceptive practiceswhere a consumer is lured into an agreement under false pretenses, only to find that the terms change or are not applied as expected. The terminology used in communicationssuch as bulk rate buy-down, off settlement, NFC, promotional rate, and rate buy-downwas introduced inconsistently by various departments involved in this transaction. Each department seemed to use a different term, with XXXX word being added to each email without clear explanation or proper definition. These terms were never properly explained or clarified in plain language, leading to confusion about their meaning and impact on the loan terms. Sales department first introduced the term bulk rate buy-down. Loan department used off settlement. Legal team referred to it as a promotional rate. Each of these terms is neither clearly defined nor standard in the industry, making it difficult for an average consumer to understand. This inconsistent use of terminology, coupled with the failure to provide clear, plain-language explanations, exemplifies the lack of transparency that violates consumer protection laws such as XXXX, RESPA, and state-specific XXXX XXXX Acts. XXXX. Unreasonable Delay in Response and Lack of Resolution Despite numerous attempts to clarify these issues directly with Lennar, including written inquiries and formal complaints, I have received no satisfactory responses. After sending legal notices and escalating the issue to higher management, there has been no acknowledgment of the serious issues I raised, nor has there been an effort to resolve the matter. The lack of response from Lennar 's legal and corporate management teams indicates either a deliberate attempt to avoid resolution or a complete failure in their customer service process. Furthermore, Lennars apology email, sent in response to my complaints, did not address the core issue of the misrepresentation of the {$21000.00} credit or the lack of clarity surrounding the loan terms. Instead, they simply apologized for the confusion without providing a substantive explanation or resolution. This apology, while seemingly conciliatory, is a clear admission of mishandling and confusion on their part. If no mistake had been made, there would have been no need for such an apology. The apology serves only as a deflection, rather than an actual resolution to the miscommunication and financial distress I have endured. This sidestepping of the original issue highlights Lennar 's failure to take responsibility for the misrepresentations and the severe financial and emotional strain they have caused. The lack of a legal or financial remedy in the apology shows that they are not addressing the real problem at handthe incorrect application of the {$21000.00} credit and the lack of clear, transparent communication surrounding the loan terms. XXXX. Impact on Financial and Emotional Well-Being As a result of these misrepresentations and the ongoing lack of transparency, my family has suffered emotional distress and confusion. The confusion surrounding the {$21000.00} credit, combined with the last-minute changes to the terms of the loan, forced me to make significant decisions under extreme pressure. This situation has caused undue financial strain, as well as emotional distress, as I was led to believe that I was receiving the agreed-upon terms and that the {$21000.00} credit would significantly reduce my loans interest rate. Furthermore, the continuous delays and lack of response have further exacerbated the anxiety and uncertainty regarding our familys home purchase. The constant back-and-forth without clear answers is unacceptable, especially given the financial implications. Applicable Legal Violations : Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) : Lennar failed to fully disclose the terms and conditions of the loan, including the exact application of the {$21000.00} credit and the promotional rate. Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ) : The lack of clear documentation regarding the application of the {$21000.00} credit violates RESPAs requirements for transparency in settlement charges. California Consumer Protection Act : Lennar 's failure to disclose critical information regarding the rate buy-down process and potential bait-and-switch tactics may constitute deceptive business practices under state law. Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ) Deceptive Advertising : Lennar may have engaged in deceptive practices by advertising the {$21000.00} credit in a way that misled consumers about its actual application and terms. State-Specific Breach of Contract Laws : The failure to fulfill the contractual promise of a {$21000.00} credit, which was a central part of my decision to purchase the home, may constitute a breach of contract under California state law. Breach of Contract and Promissory Estoppel : Lennar promised a {$21000.00} credit, which I relied upon in my decision to proceed with the purchase. The failure to deliver on this promise constitutes a breach of contract. Under the doctrine of promissory estoppel, I suffered harm from their failure to fulfill their promise. Additionally, Lennar 's last-minute suggestions to withdraw the application raise serious concerns about their lending practices. If a lender is legally obligated to act in good faith and it suggests withdrawal under duress, it casts doubt on their adherence to fair lending practices.

This is a continuation of Complaint XXXX, where among other things I requested that the servicer permit a partial reinstatement of the loan. It is not clear if the new servicer has access to, or has reviewed all of the file, or the completed loss mitigation application. That said, the current servicer continues to ignore that the loan should never have been referred to foreclosure. This is because before it was referred and placed in foreclosure I already submitted a complete loss mitigation application. The completed loss mitigation application was submitted on XX/XX/year> and the loan was referred to foreclosure XXXX days later on XX/XX/year> ( per the servicer 's records as noted in your prior response ). I have previously submitted copies of the completed loss mitigation application to the servicer. Sending my loan for foreclosure referral represents dual tracking under Regulation Z, and is not permitted which the CFPB summarizes as follows : " Servicers can not start a foreclosure proceeding if a borrower has already submitted a complete application for a loan modification or other alternative to foreclosure, and that application is still pending review. '' And this is exactly what happened here. In XXXX of 2024 I spoke with the servicer, and we went through a partial reinstatement analysis. I was initially told that the loan was eligible and that the partial reinstatement figure was {$37000.00}. As the call proceeded, however, she told me that the loan had just been referred to foreclosure and therefore it was no longer eligible. I was told that the ONLY reason my loan was ineligible for a partial reinstatement was because the loan had been referred to foreclosure. Because this is a mistake that the servicer should correct, once corrected the loan will be eligible for a partial reinstatement. Accordingly, I am not requesting a custom loss mitigation option, rather a partial reinstatement. A partial reinstatement is available from the investor regardless of default status as long as the loan is not in foreclosure. As noted above, the loan should not have been in foreclosure because a complete loss mitigation application had already been submitted. Finally, the servicer sent me a letter in XXXX of 2024 stating that I could apply for either a partial or full reinstatement. I told the servicer I again wanted a partial reinstatement. Formation and Initial Transfer of Assets : When a REMIC is initially formed, it acquires a pool of mortgages or mortgage-backed assets from a transferor, typically using a trust agreement. This transfer is often part of the REMICs creation, where the transferor places qualifying mortgages or mortgage-related assets into the REMIC structure . Form 1066, U.S. Real Estate Mortgage Investment Conduit ( REMIC ) Income Tax Return, is then used by the REMIC to report its income and tax elections but is not required to formally acquire the property. Foreclosure and Election for Foreclosure Property : When the REMIC acquires property through foreclosure or similar means ( if a borrower defaults on a mortgage within the REMIC ), it can make an election to treat the property as foreclosure property. This is done on Form 1066 by attaching a statement to the form for the tax year in which the REMIC acquires the property. This election classifies the foreclosed property as foreclosure property, which is important for favorable tax treatment, as it avoids having the income from the property treated as prohibited income for REMIC purposes. Reporting Requirements : While Form 1066 is the primary reporting form, theres no form specifically required to acquire property into the REMIC. Instead, the acquisition is documented through legal agreements and records with the trust administrator, often filed in county records for foreclosures. Schedule Q ( Form 1066 ) is also used by the REMIC to report information to residual interest holders, including details about the income and property held by the REMIC. Form 1066 Statement : This statement is an attachment to Form 1066, U.S. Real Estate Mortgage Investment Conduit ( REMIC ) Income Tax Return. It includes details about the property that the REMIC acquired through foreclosure and an explicit election under IRC 856 ( e ) to treat the property as foreclosure property. Purpose : This election allows the REMIC to classify the property as foreclosure property for tax purposes, meaning it can avoid taxes on income that would otherwise be considered non-qualifying income. Form 1099-A : Form 1099-A is issued by a lender when there is an acquisition or abandonment of secured property, typically by a financial institution to report the acquisition or abandonment of property to both the IRS and the borrower . Purpose : For the REMIC, Form 1099-A is relevant only if the REMIC must report the acquisition or abandonment of a secured property ( typically when the borrower defaults and the REMIC acquires the property ). The REMIC might use Form 1099-A to document the foreclosure for reporting purposes. According to their online system, and even when I was apparently late in paying, ( XXXX ) I did not owe any payment ( XXXX ) there was no outstanding payment due and ( XXXX ) my next payment wasn't due until XXXX. I had overpaid in XXXX so I assumed this was due to this overpayment. After I received the mark on my credit and raised this issue with XXXX, they sent me a list of phone calls they made. Unfortunately, when they made the phone calls, my wife and I were in the process of applying for a mortgage and I was receiving a ton of marketing calls from banks. Since Umpqua did not leave any personal identifying information, I did not know that the calls were regarding an issue with my HELOC. I completely relied on their online banking system and recall checking it a number of times to make sure I was up to date. I spoke with multiple employees at Umpqua who reiterated that they understand their online system is highly problematic and that it is in the process of being improved. My wife and I have a family business and we heavily rely on my credit. This mark on my credit has dropped my score about a XXXX points. Umpqua can not advertise that they have an online banking system when it is so woefully inadequate to address modern business practices. I am incredibly disappointed in their refusal to amend the mark on my credit and support small businesses like my family 's. I feel that the failed disclosure around the inadequacy of their online banking system, the failure to more quickly update their online system when they knew it is misleading, and their failure to adequately address issues like mine when harmed, are all clear consumer protection issues. CFPB staff, I am contacting you regarding a home improvement loan I took out with Wells Fargo in XX/XX/XXXX. At the time fixed rate loans were advertised at 3-4 % and I stressed I did not want an adjustable rate and wanted my loan to be a fixed rate due to the historical low rates. I went over the options with my spouse, and we decided to use fixed rate advance option to fund the repairs to our home. We returned to the bank on XX/XX/XXXX to review and sign the documents. I had lots of questions as we reviewed the contract language with the loan officer ( XXXX XXXX ). It was explained prior to signing the loan documents we could draw on our loan using fixed rate advances of money, up to three times, and those blocks would be locked in at a fixed APR. We were also given checks and a credit card that could be used but in those purchases it was explained the rate would carry a VPR tied to the prime interest rate. I asked to borrow {$5000.00} initially at a fixed rate to ensure the loan was as described but the loan officer pointed to the language in our loan contract that required fixed rate blocks to be {$10000.00} or more. We signed the contract and then took our first fixed rate block for {$25000.00} at the current fixed rate ( 3.12 % ). When I received my loan statement. I immediately checked it, and it was per the contract Fixed Rate Advance. I called the bank the following month and took another Fixed Rate Advance for {$70000.00}. I again checked the XXXX statement, ( Exhibit A ) and confirmed the 2nd loan to be fixed rate ( 2.99 % ) and the 1st loan was also correct. Over the next few years, we used the checks and credit card sparingly for miscellaneous repairs as needed knowing these would be assessed the VPR tied to the prime rate. On XX/XX/XXXX I went to the bank to do a short payoff on an auto loan I had with Wells Fargo. While talking to the banker I was advised I should refinance my Wells Fargo Home Equity loan and lock it in at a fixed rate as the prime interest rate was climbing up. I told them my understanding was the bulk of the loan was already locked in at a fixed rate, but they said the entire loan was an adjustable-rate loan. When I got home, I checked my statements and saw my rate was now listed as a VPR and the auto withdrawal against the loan had been slowly inching up over the last year as rates were moving up. I reviewed my signed contract and went back to my local bank on XX/XX/XXXX and met with a loan officer XXXX XXXX who reviewed the contract with me. She then called a corporate level loan officer, and they told us the fixed rate I was offered in XXXX was a promotional rate. XXXX XXXX went through the contract page by page and confirmed the contract we signed in XXXX does not use this term anywhere throughout the contract. Wells Fargo Corporate said they would review and send an explanation of their review of my loan in a letter. After not receiving a written explanation, I phoned Wells Fargo Corporate again on XX/XX/XXXX and again on XX/XX/XXXX trying to get this resolved. During my conversation on XX/XX/XXXX Wells Fargo pointed to language on page XX/XX/XXXX and agreed to send me a document they claimed proved I accepted the loan as a VPR loan. I never received any correspondence following that conversation. After calling them again on XX/XX/XXXX I asked for the letter, and they said they could not mail it to me, but they could send it via email. I confirmed my email with them, but they never sent me anything regarding my loan. Ive checked my account and junk mail, my spouses email accounts, and my online account but weve received nothing back from them regarding this loan. Complaint : Wells Fargo engaged in unethical behavior in the solicitation and facilitation of this loan as prohibited by TILA. Literature provided ahead of signing, Exhibit C and Exhibit D, indicated the fixed rate loans were Long Term, and the borrower could change back and forth between Fixed Rate and Variable Rate. Lender, ( Wells Fargo ) points to language on page XX/XX/XXXX ( Exhibit E ) where I supposedly requested a 12-month term for the Fixed Rate Advance. Lender ignores page XX/XX/XXXX that stipulates I must select the repayment term for the Fixed Rate Advance at the time I request the Fixed Rate Advance. No request was made for a 12-month term. Paragraph Fully Amortizing Payments ( Exhibit F ), at bottom of page XX/XX/XXXX sets term ranges for Fixed Rate Advances at 5 to 20 years so a 12-month term should never be implemented under this contract. The 2nd loan requested via phone call on XX/XX/XXXX was implemented as a Fixed Rate Loan, however I was never given the opportunity to select the term for that loan either. Lender points to language that I approved a Partially Amortizing payment option for the first loan. No such approval was given to the lender. In fact, page XXXX of a letter issued XX/XX/XXXX by the lender advising us of our conditional approval states the loan as a Line of Credit Advance Payment Type during the Draw Period : Amortizing., ( Exhibit G ). The attached notice issued clearly states This plan is being denied to to lack of self-employment documents submitted. I am not self-employed in any capacity, which has been known by Shellpoint for an extended period. There is also clear notification that loss mitigation options may be available, and you have the option to submit a complete loss mitigation application to receive a complete evaluation for all loss mitigation options available regardless of whether or not you accept this plan. Shellpoint has refused to offer any other options. Shellpoint is in violation of many CFPB laws relating to loss mitigation and loan modifications, primarily CFPB 1024.41. Shellpoint has been stalling out the process for many months unnecessarily. The rules listed below clarify the obligations of Shellpoint. 1024.41 ( c ) ( 4 ) ( ii ) ( B ) ( 4 ) Denial of loan modification options. If a borrower 's complete loss mitigation application is denied for any trial or permanent loan modification option available to the borrower pursuant to paragraph ( c ) of this section, a servicer shall state in the notice sent to the borrower pursuant to paragraph ( c ) ( 1 ) ( ii ) of this section the specific reason or reasons for the servicer & # 39 ; s determination for each such trial or permanent loan modification option and, if applicable, that the borrower was not evaluated on other criteria. Furthermore, SLS has not provided a full accounting breakdown to prove up the validity of the debt. I have requested this information on numerous occasions via qualified written request QWR. The QWR request has issues raised regarding deed and title transfers that have not 2 been responded too. Per 12 CFR 1024.36, SLS is required to respond based on HUD law. 12 CFR 1024.36 - Requests for information. ( a ) Information request. A servicer shall comply with the requirements of this section for any written request for information from a borrower that includes the name of the borrower, information that enables the servicer to identify the borrower & # 39 ; s mortgage loan account, and states the information the borrower is requesting with respect to the borrower & # 39 ; s mortgage loan. A request on a payment coupon or other payment form supplied by the servicer need not be treated by the servicer as a request for information. A request for a payoff balance need not be treated by the servicer as a request for information. A qualified written request that requests information relating to the servicing of the mortgage loan is a request for information for purposes of this section, and a servicer must comply with all requirements applicable to a request for information with respect to such qualified written request. ( ii ) Extension of time limit. For requests for information governed by the time limit set forth in paragraph ( d ) ( 2 ) ( i ) ( B ) of this section, a servicer may extend the time period for responding by an additional 15 days ( excluding legal public holidays, Saturdays, and Sun days ) if, before the end of the 30- day period, the servicer notifies the borrower of the extension and the reasons for the extension in writing. A servicer may not extend the time period for requests for information governed by paragraph ( d ) ( 2 ) ( i ) ( A ) of this section. Based on the information submitted within, I am seeking your assistance on this matter.

I am writing to file a formal complaint against Freedom Mortgage Corporation ( FMC ) regarding its egregious mismanagement of my mortgage account, which has caused significant financial hardship, emotional stress, and systemic violations of federal regulations. Despite months of diligent communication and compliance on my part, FMC has failed to address my concerns adequately, leaving me with unresolved issues dating back to XX/XX/year>2024. Below is a detailed chronology of the mishandling and regulatory violations : 1. Mishandling of Forbearance Requests XXXX 2024 : I submitted a forbearance application ( more than once ) with all required documents and was assured by FMC representatives that the process would take 710 days. Months later, I was only informed my documents were " missing, '' forcing me to resubmit them multiple times because I had to reach out to FMC directly and ask what is going on. During this time, I sent numerous statements via fax and FMCs secure messaging portal, none of which elicited a substantive response. XX/XX/year>2024 : After six months of relentless efforts, I received written confirmation of a Special Forbearance Program, suspending payments until XX/XX/year>. However, FMC revoked this forbearance ( via letter ) without explanation on XX/XX/scrub> 2024, undermining the promised relief and exacerbating my financial instability. I sent countless statements seeking clarity and receive no response. 2. Contradictory and Arbitrary Information XXXX 2024 : FMC representatives assured me that payments for XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX were deferred. Subsequently, I was blindsided by a previously undisclosed " 210-day seasoning requirement, '' invalidating the deferral and further deepening my financial challenges. This was confirmed by a FMC representative, XXXX XXXX who listened to the calls and told me that she was sorry I was given the wrong information and that they reps who provided the incorrect information have been addressed. XX/XX/year>2024 : Despite confirming my forbearance approval, I was repeatedly informed by FMC representatives that my case required further " review, '' delaying resolution. 3. Escalating and Unexplained Mortgage Balance My mortgage balance inexplicably increased to {$26000.00} by XX/XX/year>2024 from the agreed-upon amount of {$13000.00}. This includes erroneous fees and charges that FMC has failed to justify or address. I was told by a loss mitigation representative that once my forbearance is granted, the balance will stay at the {$13000.00} until XX/XX/year>2024 this is confirmed on a call the Freedom Mortgage. 4. Failure to Enroll in VA Special Programs Despite guidance from FMC representatives in XX/XX/year>2024, to pursue the VA Special Programs ( VASP ) for loan modification ( adding 10 years to term ) and interest rate adjustment ( 2.5 % ) which I requested XXXX 2024, FMC failed to facilitate or confirm my enrollment. 5. Ineffectiveness of VA Loan Guaranty Service In my efforts to resolve these issues, I contacted the VA Loan Guaranty Service and have been working with XXXX XXXX. Unfortunately, this service has proven to be more of a liaison with limited capacity to enforce meaningful changes. While I appreciate their assistance, it has not provided the resolution needed for the hardship FMC has caused. 6. Regulatory Violations FMC 's actions constitute clear violations of the following federal regulations : Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ) : FMC failed to provide timely and accurate information regarding forbearance requests, violating Regulation X. Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) : FMC neglected to disclose changes to loan terms, including the arbitrary imposition of a " 210-day seasoning requirement. '' Dodd-Frank Act ( UDAAP ) : FMC engaged in unfair, deceptive, and abusive practices through misleading communication and arbitrary policy changes. 38 CFR Part 36 : FMC failed to provide adequate loss mitigation options and special forbearance protections for VA-backed loans. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Mortgage Servicing Rules : FMC failed to evaluate and communicate loss mitigation options clearly, as required by CFPB regulations. 7. Emotional and Financial Impact As a 100 % disabled combat veteran, the negligence displayed by FMC has caused significant emotional distress and financial uncertainty. I have made every effort to be proactive since XX/XX/year>2024, informing FMC about my impending financial difficulties and seeking a collaborative resolution. Instead, FMCs sheer incompetence has directly caused this financial hardship, negatively impacting both me and my family. Immediate Requests for Resolution To rectify these issues, I request the following immediate actions I have been requesting these actions for days shy of 2 months with XXXX response from FMC : 1. Reinstate and Honor Forbearance Terms : Reinstate the terms outlined in FMCs letter dated XX/XX/scrub> 2024, suspending payments until XX/XX/scrub> 2024. 2. Adjust Mortgage Balance : Correct my mortgage balance to reflect the agreed-upon amount of {$13000.00}, removing any erroneous charges and fees. 3. VA Special Programs Enrollment : Expedite my enrollment in the VASP program to modify my loan terms by extending the term ( 10 years ) and reducing the interest rate ( 2.5 % ) as advised by FMC representatives. 4. Deferral of Missed Payments : Defer all missed payments to the end of the mortgage term. 5. Single Point of Contact : Assign a competent representative to provide consistent and reliable communication to resolve these ongoing issues. Supporting Documentation I have attached the following documents to substantiate my claims : 1. Formal correspondence with FMC, highlighting regulatory violations and mismanagement. 2. FMCs decision letters, including contradictory statements and policy shifts. 3. Timeline of phone calls and written inquiries that demonstrate the persistent lack of accountability and resolution by FMC. 4. Relevant excerpts from federal regulations applicable to my case. Conclusion FMCs actions reflect a systemic failure to comply with regulatory standards and fulfill its obligations to its customers. I urge the CFPB to investigate this matter thoroughly and take appropriate actions to hold FMC accountable. I trust that your office will ensure justice and protect other consumers from similar misconduct. Thank you for your attention to this urgent matter. I am available for further clarification or to provide additional evidence if needed.

I am writing in response and requesting a NEW INVESTIGATION into the deception that was submitted that was submitted to the CFPB Complaint # XXXX, the letter dated XX/XX/XXXX, regarding M & T Banks failure to acknowledge and honor my timely filed rescission request, which was sent to them on XX/XX/XXXX, concerning my mortgage account # XXXX for the property located at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX IL XXXX. M & T Banks failure to recognize and act upon the letter of rescission is not only a violation of federal law but also a direct contradiction to the clear and unequivocal guidelines set forth by the United States Supreme Court. Specifically, in the case Jesinoski v. Countrywide Home Loans , Inc., 135 S. Ct. 790 ( 2015 ), the Court held that a borrowers rescission of a mortgage loan under the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) is effective once the rescission notice is mailed to the lender or servicer. The Court ruled that the borrower is not required to provide any further explanation or justification for the rescission, and the rescission becomes effective immediately upon mailing. M & T Bank has disregarded this law by failing to acknowledge that my rescission notice was properly mailed on XX/XX/XXXX, in accordance with 15 U.S.C. 1635 and the Supreme Court 's ruling in Jesinoski. As the law clearly states, rescission is automatic and effective upon mailing, and M & T Banks continued failure to comply with my lawful request constitutes a violation of both federal law and the protections afforded to borrowers under TILA. Additionally, the Illinois state laws also support my position. Under 815 ILCS 505/2, the Illinois Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act, consumers are protected from unfair business practices, including a failure to honor a legally binding rescission. Furthermore, under Illinois case law, including Williams v. Ameribank, 330 Ill. App. 3d 537 ( 2002 ), Illinois courts have affirmed that once a rescission notice is mailed in accordance with TILA, it is valid and enforceable without the lender 's further consent. I am deeply concerned by M & T Banks refusal to comply with this legal obligation. The failure to recognize my timely and lawful rescission is causing me significant distress and potentially exposing me to continued financial harm. The law is clear : my rescission is effective immediately, and I request that the CFPB take immediate action to ensure that M & T Bank adheres to the legal requirements of rescission under both federal and Illinois state law. I respectfully request that the CFPB require M & T Bank to : Acknowledge and honor my rescission notice. Provide written confirmation that the rescission has been processed and that the loan has been terminated. Reverse any fees or charges related to this mortgage account that have been applied since the date of the rescission. Thank you for your attention to this urgent matter. I look forward to your prompt response and intervention to enforce my rights under the law.

For example, here is one I worked on today '', and showed an image that had " walls-in '' on the declaration page, thus directly admitting that the only reason the lender isn't accepting the insurance is that the word " walls-in '' doesn't appear on the declarations page. The declarations page lists " Building ( Blanket ) '' and " Building '' is later defined in the document to include the building or structure, additions, fixtures, building glass, additions under construction, appliances, floor coverings, alterations and repairs to the building and structure, and many other things. By any reasonable interpretation of " walls-in '' ( including the interpretation of two insurance agents and the HOA community XXXX ), it is clear that the HOA insurance policy provides " walls-in '' coverage and that the HOA CC & Rs require the HOA to maintain " walls-in '' coverage. The appraisal concluded that my homes value and condition met FNMAs underwriting standards and that there were no conditions attached to the appraisal. This conclusion is consistent with the appraisal conducted just 12 months ago when I originally purchased the home. Subsequently, XXXX XXXX underwriting team informed me that I must install a handrail on a flat-top roof due to door access. While this may be required under current building codes for new construction, my property is grandfathered under local building codes, as the area in question has not been altered. Moreover, the appraisal explicitly stated that no handrail was necessary. When I inquired about the basis for this requirement and requested clarification regarding the underwriting guidelines necessitating such an improvement, XXXX XXXX underwriting team repeatedly stated that it was their internal requirement. No specific guidance or justification aligned with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX was provided. I informed them that conditioning the loan on installing a handrail would eliminate any of the economics of using them based on their rate. I furthermore conducted research and consulted with underwriters from other financial institutions, all of which indicated that XXXX XXXX requirement exceeds FNMAs guidelines. XXXX XXXX underwriting team even asserted that, Underwriting calls for items deemed safety concerns even on as-is reports ; we dont need the appraisers input in such instances. However, according to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, Section B4-1.3-06, Property Condition and Quality of Construction of the Improvements, underwriting decisions are to be based on the appraisal report, which, in this instance, explicitly noted no conditions requiring a handrail. This leads me to conclude that XXXX XXXX underwriting team is imposing requirements that exceed XXXX XXXX guidelines and are based on subjective internal policies rather than objective criteria established by XXXX. Furthermore, under the Truth in Lending Act, any additional conditions or standards imposed by a lender beyond those required by the GSEs must be adequately disclosed. Upon discussing this matter with my loan officer, I was assured that my application was not subject to standards exceeding FNMAs guidelines. However, XXXX XXXX actions suggest otherwise, as they are conditioning my loan approval on adherence to internal standards rather than the guidelines to which my loan should be underwritten.

I have been making XXXX of my mortgage payment, plus additional money to be applied to the principal, every XXXX weeks. I have been doing this via the autopayment option on my mortgage. The concept of paying with greater frequency ( without making overpaymemnts ) to pay down your principal has been proven to remove years from the term ( almost 5 years from a 30 year term ). In my case, I am also making ( 1 ) extra payment annually towards the principal ( 26 half payments annually, plus some additional money that is supposed to go straight towards the principal amount. Chase, does not apply funds when received towards my mortgage. The first half of the payment, including the portion earmarked specifically for principal from Chase 's auto payment center, sits in the mortgage account not collecting interest as it might in bank account, and not being applied towards the mortgage until the second half of the monthly mortgage payment is received. Once both half payments are recieved, the payment is applied to the mortgage balance, and the principal overpayment is also applied. This seems like a deliberately misleading process. The point of making payments every 2 weeks is to pay the principal down when each payment is made. Upon speaking with the Vermont Attorney Generals Office, I was advised to contact you to submit this formal complaint to bring to your attention the inhumane and unfair practices of Wells Fargo Mortgage Service, which have caused significant distress and hardship following my husbands passing. My husband and I have held several mortgages with Wells Fargo in the past. Our most recent mortgage was taken out in XX/XX/year>. At that time, we were advised by the institution not to include my name on the mortgage note, as I was not working. Trusting their guidance, we proceeded. However, our attorney at the XX/XX/year> closing expressed concern about this arrangement, particularly regarding potential issues if anything were to happen to my husband. At his insistence, I signed the mortgage during the closing, and my name is also on the deed. We believed this resolved any concerns. For nine years, we paid the mortgage without issue. After my husbands passing, I continued to make payments via the online account. However, in XXXX, after paying the XXXX installment, I called Wells Fargo to ask a question and mentioned my husbands passing. I was transferred to the " Life Events '' department and informed that I no longer had access to the account. This marked the beginning of an ongoing nightmare : 1. Locked Out of Online Access : Despite my continued payments, my online access was revoked, and I was directed to call the Life Events department. They promised to send information on my options, but this was either not sent or sent to an outdated address, despite my efforts to correct my contact information. 2. Insensitivity and Miscommunication : Representatives repeatedly called my late husbands phone, leaving messages for him. When I expressed frustration, I was treated with a lack of empathy, accused ( in a loud and harsh tone ) of using my deceased husband to access his account, and subjected to condescending remarks. 3. Unreasonable Fees for Mortgage Assumption : The initial several phone calls led me to believe that assuming the mortgage would simply require me to qualify and assume the same rate. It wasnt until much later that I was informed that I could assume the mortgage for a nominal fee. After being very evasive and hearing multiple stories, this turned out to be over {$11000.00}. I was also offered the option to refinance at a significantly higher interest rate, which I declined as it was financially unreasonable. 4. Inaccessibility of Payment Options : Without online access, I was told to pay in person at the nearest Wells Fargo branchover three hours awayor mail payments, which my attorney strongly advised against due to concerns about check fraud. On multiple occasions, I drove over six hours round trip to make payments in person, only to encounter errors in how the payments were applied. XXXX payment is already wrong, and funds have repeatedly been misapplied to different months and the principal. Without access to an online account, it is impossible to keep track of the payments and confirm they have applied they have been applied correctly. 5. Rude and Unhelpful Customer Service : A bank rep asked me on the phone whether or not I could even pay the mortgage in a condescending tone and told me to just pay it off at once, which is not her place. During one visit, a representative assured me the payment was correctly applied but later admitted it was not, requiring a case to be opened. The lack of attention to detail and accountability has been deeply frustrating and time-consuming. The treatment I have received as a grieving widow and senior citizen is unacceptable. The death of a spouse is one of the most difficult life events, and Wells Fargo has compounded my distress through mismanagement, lack of transparency, and disrespect. Additionally, I am concerned about possible fraudulent practices. Our copy of the mortgage documentation indicates that I signed the mortgage ( see the provided XXXX - XXXX ), but Wells Fargo appears to have obscured this information. This raises serious questions about their integrity and compliance. Attached to this complaint, you will find documentation supporting my claims, including evidence of my signature on the mortgage, records of my payments, a copy of a check I made for a second down payment on the home, and correspondence with Wells Fargo representatives. Vermont is a right-of-survivorship state so long as the couple is married and residing together in the home at the time of death, which was the case with my husband and me at his time of death. I am simply asking for reasonable and consistent access to make payments on my mortgage without the undue burden of excessive fees or unnecessary travel. Wells Fargos conduct has caused me significant emotional stress, and I urge the CFPB to investigate these practices. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Despite this proactive step, the new mortgage company sent a demand for payment, even though I am currently in the midst of a XXXX XXXX bankruptcy proceeding. This demand for payment may violate federal bankruptcy protections, as such actions could constitute an attempt to collect a debt during an automatic stay. Further complicating matters, the mortgage in question had already been modified prior to the servicing transfer. The trial payments for the modification were all made on time, and the prior servicer sent the finalized modification paperwork via FedEx. The documents were signed and returned as required, and the agreement was considered complete. Despite this, the new mortgage servicer issued a demand for the pre-modification balance, disregarding the agreed-upon terms of the modification. Adding to the gravity of the situation, the demand for payment was sent to the property address, which has never been the designated mailing address. This act resulted in the dissemination of private and non-public personal information ( NPI ) to an unauthorized address, potentially constituting a violation of my privacy rights and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). Potential Legal Violations and Relevant Federal Statutes Below are the potential legal issues and the corresponding statutes that could be cited. It is important to note that these interpretations are offered with caution, and legal counsel should be consulted for definitive advice. 1. Violation of Automatic Stay under Bankruptcy Law Statute : 11 U.S.C. 362 ( a ) Explanation : During a XXXX XXXX bankruptcy, an automatic stay is in place, prohibiting creditors from attempting to collect on debts without permission from the bankruptcy court. Sending a demand for payment under these circumstances may be considered a violation of the automatic stay provisions. 2. Failure to Honor Terms of Mortgage Modification Potential Issue : Breach of contract Explanation : If the mortgage modification was legally executed and finalized, issuing a demand for the pre-modification balance could be construed as a breach of contract. This may not directly involve a federal statute but could raise concerns under state contract law. 3. Violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) Statute : 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( f ) Explanation : Under the FCRA, entities are required to safeguard non-public personal information ( NPI ). By sending sensitive financial information to an incorrect and unauthorized address, the new servicer may have violated these provisions, potentially exposing personal data to unauthorized parties. 4. Breach of Privacy and Non-Public Personal Information Protections Statute : Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act ( GLBA ), 15 U.S.C. 6801 ( b ) Explanation : Financial institutions are obligated to protect the confidentiality of customer information. Disclosing private details to an unauthorized address could represent a failure to uphold these obligations, potentially violating the GLBA. 5. Unfair or Deceptive Acts or Practices ( UDAP ) Statute : 15 U.S.C. 45 ( Federal Trade Commission Act ) Explanation : If the demand for payment is deemed misleading or deceptive, it may fall under the scope of UDAP provisions, which prohibit unfair or deceptive practices in commerce.
